tools.name: AJ Bell
tools.summary: AJ Bell is a broad UK investment platform covering taxable, ISA, LISA, junior, company, trust, and pension accounts. It combines percentage account charges with capped listed-asset custody, £5 share dealing, £1.50 fund dealing, and tiered FX. It is strongest for account breadth and long-term administration rather than commission-free trading.

tools.name: Ziggma
tools.summary: Ziggma is a web-based portfolio tracker and investment research workspace for self-directed investors who want account consolidation, stock and ETF screening, dividend tracking, portfolio checkups, smart alerts, impact analysis, and idea lists in one place. It fits users comparing portfolio tracker and stock portfolio tracker tools, especially when they want broker-agnostic monitoring rather than a trading app. Free access covers core research with limits; paid tiers unlock more broker links, stock scores, alerts, optimizer tools, model and guru portfolios, and larger virtual-portfolio workflows. It is not a broker, registered investment advisor, tax-lot accounting system, or full global market-data terminal.

tools.name: getquin
tools.summary: getquin is a consumer portfolio and net-worth tracker for investors who want broker and bank connections, multi-asset portfolio tracking, dividend views, AI portfolio analysis, retirement planning, budgeting, liabilities, insurance tracking, and a social investing community in one web and mobile app. It is strongest for European retail investors who want a mobile-first overview across brokers, wallets, assets, and community ideas. Premium exists through in-app subscription, but exact public feature gating and regional pricing should be checked before comparing paid plans.

tools.name: Delta by eToro
tools.summary: Delta by eToro is a multi-asset portfolio tracker for stocks, ETFs, funds, crypto, NFTs, forex, commodities, indices, brokers, exchanges, and wallets. It is useful when you want one read-only portfolio view across accounts and asset classes rather than another place to trade.

tools.name: Kubera
tools.summary: Kubera is a paid net-worth and portfolio tracker for high-net-worth households, founders, expats, advisors, and family-office style users who need one balance-sheet view across bank accounts, brokerages, crypto, real estate, private-company equity, alternatives, documents, beneficiaries, and multiple currencies. It supports global account aggregation, scenario modeling, document storage, estate handoff workflows, white-label advisor portals, and a first-party API. It is tracking and reporting software, not a broker, tax engine, trading/rebalancing execution system, or free personal-finance app.

tools.name: Quicken (Simplifi & Classic)
tools.summary: Quicken is personal finance software with investment tracking layered into household budgeting, tax, retirement, and account-aggregation workflows. Simplifi is the web and mobile path for real-time portfolio tracking, IRR/TWR, holdings-based news, and retirement projections, while Quicken Classic adds deeper desktop investing, tax-lot, capital-gains, Portfolio Analyzer, Portfolio X-Ray, and tax-reporting workflows. It is strongest for U.S. and Canadian households that want investments connected to the rest of their finances. It is not a broker, trading platform, professional research terminal, public API, or best fit for investors outside the U.S. and Canada.

tools.name: Masttro
tools.summary: Masttro is an enterprise wealth operating system for UHNW families, single-family offices, multi-family offices, RIAs, private banks, and professional-services firms that need consolidated reporting across custodians, entities, currencies, alternatives, documents, compliance, client portals, and AI-assisted workflows. It is built for complex wealth operations, not self-directed retail portfolio tracking. Pricing is quote-based, fixed annual licensing rather than AUM-based, and evaluation normally requires a demo and implementation scoping.

tools.name: SS&C Black Diamond Wealth Solutions
tools.summary: SS&C Black Diamond Wealth Solutions is an enterprise wealth-management platform for RIAs, broker-dealers, family offices, banks, and trust teams that need portfolio accounting, performance reporting, client portals, billing, trading and rebalancing, data aggregation, APIs, compliance, alternatives, trust services, and modular operations support. It is strongest for advisory firms running complex client books, but pricing is sales-led and many capabilities are separately scoped modules rather than a lightweight retail portfolio app.

tools.name: Börsdata
tools.summary: Börsdata is a Nordic-first equity analytics, screening, and data platform for investors who want long-history fundamentals, thousands of ratios, strategy screens, ownership data, insider and short-selling context, technical charts, reports, watchlists, calendars, and API or spreadsheet access. It is strongest for Nordic stock research, while global coverage, holdings data, Excel/Sheets workflows, and REST API access depend on paid tiers and professional users are routed to Enterprise.

tools.name: Addepar
tools.summary: Addepar is an enterprise wealth and investment management platform for RIAs, family offices, private banks, asset managers, and institutions that need multi-asset portfolio accounting, reporting, trading, client portals, alternatives workflows, APIs, and firm-wide data infrastructure. It is strongest as a professional portfolio system of record, not a self-serve retail research app, and pricing, modules, integrations, market data, and implementation scope are sales-led.

tools.name: Envestnet Wealth Management Platform
tools.summary: Envestnet Wealth Management Platform is an enterprise wealthtech ecosystem for RIAs, broker-dealers, banks, asset managers, and fintechs. It is useful when a firm needs advisor workflows across planning, proposals, trading, reporting, billing, client portals, data, APIs, and integrations rather than a self-directed investing app.

tools.name: Orion Advisor Tech
tools.summary: Orion Advisor Tech is enterprise infrastructure for RIAs and wealth firms that need portfolio accounting, billing, reporting, tax-aware trading, CRM, planning, compliance, risk analytics, client portals, APIs, and data infrastructure under one operating stack. Public stack pricing starts in the five figures per year and module access depends on the selected Orion Stack or standalone products. It is not a self-serve portfolio tracker, consumer research app, discount broker, or low-cost tool for individual investors.

tools.name: Letters and Reviews
tools.summary: Letters and Reviews is a free personal curation site for fund manager letters, hedge fund letters, shareholder letters, ticker mentions, and quarterly 13F pages. It is useful for value investors and researchers who want a lightweight starting point for primary-source idea generation before reading the original manager commentary or filing. Letters and Reviews is a curated link hub, not a normalized holdings database, alerting product, full-text research platform, or investment recommendation service.

tools.name: Office of Financial Research (U.S. Treasury)
tools.summary: Office of Financial Research is a free U.S. Treasury source for official financial-stability monitors, stress indicators, short-term funding data, money-market fund transparency, bank systemic-risk views, and hedge-fund monitor datasets. It is useful for macro, risk, policy, and market-structure research where documented methodology and public JSON or CSV access matter more than a polished investing app. OFR data is generally monitor-specific and often end-of-day or lagged. It is not a real-time market-data feed, stock research terminal, broker, portfolio tracker, or broad trading dataset.

tools.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York - Data & Statistics
tools.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Data & Statistics is an official source for U.S. reference rates, markets operations data, SOMA holdings, primary dealer statistics, survey data, and research indicators. It is useful when investors, economists, and data teams need authoritative SOFR, EFFR, OBFR, funding-market, Treasury, agency MBS, and macro indicator data with exportable formats and public API access. It provides source data rather than an analytics product, stock screener, broker, portfolio tracker, alerting system, or full market-data terminal.

tools.name: Yellowbrick Investing
tools.summary: Yellowbrick Investing is a stock-idea and hedge-fund-holdings research platform for investors who want searchable pitches, investor feeds, 13F-based fund activity, daily idea emails, and a premium model portfolio workflow. It fits users looking for hedge fund stock ideas or a stock pitch platform, but its value is in sourcing research leads rather than replacing diligence. Free access is delayed and limited; Premium unlocks real-time ideas, professional portfolios, enhanced filters, investor return stats, and portfolio trade alerts. It is not a broker, registered adviser, portfolio accounting system, public API, or guarantee that copied ideas will work.

tools.name: Smartkarma
tools.summary: Smartkarma is a premium investment intelligence platform for professional investors, asset managers, banks, and accredited/private investors who need independent research, specialist analysts, data tools, watchlists, and real-time alerts. A Preview Pass provides limited discovery, while Pro is documented at USD 10,950/year per user and Premium/Data or Plus access can require request or onboarding workflows. It is not a retail stock screener, broker, portfolio accounting system, or low-cost news site.

tools.name: In Practise
tools.summary: In Practise is a qualitative investment research library built around executive interviews, transcripts, surveys, and company learning journeys for long-term fundamental investors. It is useful when you want business-model context, operating detail, customer or competitor insight, and management-level perspective to complement filings, earnings transcripts, and valuation work. The free plan gives a limited way to sample the library, while full access and private interview workflows are paid and sales-led.

tools.name: Find and update company information (Companies House)
tools.summary: Companies House Find and update company information is the official free UK company register for searching companies, filings, officers, ownership-control records, and document images. It supports UK due diligence, private-company checks, filing alerts, and developer workflows that need primary-source registry data rather than analyst commentary.

tools.name: Diffchecker
tools.summary: Diffchecker is a document-comparison tool for text, Word files, PDFs, Excel files, images, folders, APIs, and desktop workflows. Use it in investing work when you need fast redlines for filings, research drafts, models, contracts, or disclosure changes, not when you need financial data itself.

tools.name: Strike.Market
tools.summary: Strike.Market is a free equity research and stock screener site that combines fundamentals with alternative-data signals such as website traffic, app rankings, social followers, Google Trends, job postings, patents, insider trading, institutional ownership, analyst targets, and earnings calendars. It fits users searching for a free stock screener or alternative data screener, especially when they want nontraditional signals before checking filings and fundamentals. Optional sign-in adds personalized feeds and alerts, and the site offers embeddable earnings-calendar widgets. It is not a broker, portfolio accounting product, enterprise data feed, or source with verified SLA and freshness guarantees.

tools.name: Portseido
tools.summary: Portseido is a global investment portfolio tracker for self-directed investors who want transaction-based performance, dividend tracking, allocation views, risk metrics, benchmarking, lot analysis, multi-currency support, and custom assets across web and mobile. Free and Plus are useful for smaller portfolios, while Pro removes transaction limits and supports multiple portfolios after a no-card trial. It is not a broker, live broker-sync product, public API, tax filing system, or advisor-grade rebalancing platform.

tools.name: Zenvesto
tools.summary: Zenvesto is a web-based stock, ETF, crypto, and benchmark portfolio tracker built around dashboards, watchlists, performance metrics, portfolio health scoring, AI-powered insights, market news, earnings calendars, CSV imports, and historical simulation. It fits stock portfolio tracker and AI portfolio tracker intent, but current public evidence supports conservative U.S. exchange coverage, finite plan limits, and manual or CSV workflows rather than broker sync. It is useful when a modern dashboard and guided analysis matter more than tax-grade accounting or execution. It is not a broker, public API today, custodian sync product, wash-sale engine, or professional portfolio accounting system.

tools.name: Wealth Hub - Hedge Fund Letters
tools.summary: Wealth Hub Hedge Fund Letters is a free public index of hedge fund investor letters and 13-F report links organized by quarter. It is useful for value investors, analysts, and students who want manager commentary, idea generation, and original letter archives before doing their own filing and valuation work. It provides discovery and source access rather than a normalized research database, structured holdings platform, full-text search engine, alerting product, public API, or recommendation service.

tools.name: Google Trends
tools.summary: Google Trends is a free search-interest research tool for investors, operators, marketers, and analysts who want to monitor attention, demand proxies, brand momentum, consumer themes, and news-driven spikes across regions and time. It is strongest as context: search interest can support alternative-data research, but the values are normalized relative indexes rather than exact query volumes or revenue data. The web UI is broadly available, while official API access is limited and the BigQuery dataset covers selected top and rising queries.

tools.name: Ahrefs
tools.summary: Ahrefs is an SEO and marketing intelligence platform that investors can use as alternative data for digital businesses, marketplaces, publishers, SaaS companies, and consumer brands where search visibility and web demand matter. It is strongest for website traffic estimates, keyword demand, backlinks, content visibility, API exports, and AI-brand visibility, but it is not an investing terminal, valuation model, portfolio tracker, or source of official company fundamentals.

tools.name: ApeWisdom
tools.summary: ApeWisdom is a free social-sentiment and ticker-attention tracker for traders and researchers watching Reddit, WallStreetBets-style communities, crypto subreddits, and 4chan /biz. It is strongest for spotting retail attention and meme-stock chatter early, with public leaderboards and API endpoints, but ticker mentions are noisy and should not be treated as investment quality or price direction.

tools.name: AUM 13F
tools.summary: AUM 13F is a due-diligence web app for researching asset managers, institutional holdings, private funds, real estate managers, and limited-partner relationships from public filing sources. It is strongest for analysts who want a low-cost way to browse manager AUM, 13F holdings, EDGAR filings, IAPD records, CAFR-sourced LP portfolios, source links, portfolios, and alerts, but 13F data remains delayed and incomplete by design.

tools.name: 13F Insight
tools.summary: 13F Insight is an SEC-filings intelligence platform for investors who want to track institutional 13F holdings, Form 4 insider trades, 13D/G ownership, watchlists, smart-money alerts, and AI answers grounded in filing citations. It is strongest for hedge-fund and institutional-ownership research, but 13F filings are delayed by design and AI summaries should be checked against the underlying SEC documents.

tools.name: Similarweb
tools.summary: Similarweb is a digital intelligence and website traffic analytics platform for researching web traffic, app usage, keywords, referrals, competitors, companies, technologies, and online market share. For investors, it provides alternative data for digital businesses such as marketplaces, ecommerce, SaaS, media, travel, and consumer internet, not reported financials. Meaningful API, history, exports, integrations, and enterprise workflows are paid or custom. It is not a broker, portfolio tracker, valuation model, fundamentals terminal, or direct source of company revenue.

tools.name: Sensor Tower
tools.summary: Sensor Tower is a sales-led mobile app, advertising, gaming, web, and audience intelligence platform for analysts who use app downloads, usage, revenue estimates, ad creatives, audience behavior, and web/app trends as alternative data. Public charts and app lookup tools support lightweight discovery; commercial workflows use Sensor Tower Connect, APIs, scheduled feeds, Snowflake, Salesforce, Slack, and custom alerts. It is not a stock screener, fundamentals database, portfolio tracker, broker, or direct source of reported company revenue.

tools.name: Semrush
tools.summary: Semrush is an SEO, marketing intelligence, website traffic analytics, and AI search visibility platform that investors can use as alternative data for search-dependent companies, publishers, agencies, ecommerce, SaaS, and consumer brands. It supports keyword demand, competitor visibility, traffic proxies, and channel analysis; these modeled signals require validation against filings and first-party metrics. It is a marketing platform rather than investing software, not a broker, portfolio tracker, valuation model, official fundamentals provider, or direct measure of company revenue.

tools.name: Hunter
tools.summary: Hunter is an email finder, verification, enrichment, and outreach platform for analysts, founders, sales teams, and deal teams that need professional contact discovery around companies and domains. It can support investment research when the workflow requires expert outreach, customer discovery, diligence interviews, or partnership sourcing, but it is not an investing data source. Usage is credit-based, API-enabled, and compliance-sensitive: users still need lawful outreach practices, opt-out handling, and deliverability controls.

tools.name: Stock Spinoff Investing
tools.summary: Stock Spinoff Investing is a niche research site and paid newsletter for investors focused on spin-offs and related special situations. Its free value is the upcoming and completed spin-off calendar; SSI Premium adds roughly one new idea per month, weekly updates, live monthly video Q&A, Discord access, and historical newsletters. It is not a broad stock research terminal, portfolio construction tool, broker, public API, or substitute for filing review and independent valuation.

tools.name: FlightAware
tools.summary: FlightAware is a global flight-tracking platform and aviation data provider, useful to investors when flight activity, delays, routes, airports, airlines, logistics, business travel, or private aviation can act as alternative data. It is strongest as aviation operations infrastructure: free web and mobile tracking handle consumer lookup, while AeroAPI, Firehose, Foresight, FlightAware Global, and Rapid Reports support developer, enterprise, and one-off data workflows. It is not a financial-data terminal, so any investment use case should connect flight signals back to sector-specific research.

tools.name: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX)
tools.summary: HKEX is the official Hong Kong exchange source for listed-company announcements, HKEXnews filings, corporate calendars, market alerts, delayed public quotes, and licensed market data services. It is strongest when investors and data teams need primary-source Hong Kong disclosures or official exchange feeds rather than third-party summaries. Public pages are useful and free, but real-time, historical tick, full order book, and redistribution workflows require paid HKEX Market Data Services, Data Marketplace products, and licensing.

tools.name: camelcamelcamel (UK)
tools.summary: camelcamelcamel UK is a free Amazon price-tracking site for shoppers, ecommerce researchers, and consumer-products analysts who want Amazon UK price-history charts, price-drop alerts, wishlist imports, RSS, bookmarklets, and the Camelizer browser extension. It is useful for product-pricing context and purchase timing, but it is an Amazon consumer tool rather than a company fundamentals platform, market-data feed, or investment research terminal.

tools.name: CB Insights
tools.summary: CB Insights is an enterprise market-intelligence platform for strategy, innovation, venture, corporate development, M&A, and investment teams researching private companies, public companies, investors, deals, markets, business relationships, and competitive signals. It is strongest for private-market intelligence, AI-assisted scouting, market maps, predictive scores, and workflow integrations, but pricing is request-based and data feeds or enterprise integrations require commercial scope.

tools.name: SecForm4.Com
tools.summary: SecForm4.com is a U.S. insider trading and ownership monitoring site for Form 4, Forms 3 and 5, 13D/13G, and 13F filings from EDGAR. It fits users searching for SecForm4, insider trading trackers, Form 4 activity, and 13D/13G monitoring, with free public access and advanced ownership views for power users. The right use case is monitoring SEC filing signals before checking transaction context, issuer fundamentals, and current ownership. It is not a broker, global insider-disclosure database, portfolio tracker, public API, or standalone buy/sell signal.

tools.name: Fintel
tools.summary: Fintel is a market-signal research platform for investors who want short interest, off-exchange volume, institutional ownership, insider trades, ETF exposure, options sentiment, filings, screeners, dashboards, alerts, APIs, and AI-assisted research in one place. It is strongest for ticker-level signal pages and ownership/short-interest workflows that help explain positioning, crowding, and unusual activity before deeper fundamental work. Many premium datasets, AI workflows, exports, options flow, and portfolio tools are tier-gated, and the signals should be treated as research inputs rather than investment recommendations.

tools.name: IBorrowDesk
tools.summary: IBorrowDesk is a stock-borrow availability and borrow-fee tracker built around Interactive Brokers reported securities-lending data. It is useful for short sellers, event-driven traders, and researchers who want to monitor borrow availability, fee changes, and hard-to-borrow pressure on stocks and ETFs. The key limitation is scope: IBorrowDesk reflects IBKR availability and fees only, not the whole securities-lending market, and longer history or CSV exports require Patron support.

tools.name: Invesst
tools.summary: Invesst is an AI-first investing workspace for RIAs, portfolio managers, analysts, and serious self-directed investors who want natural-language research, stock and ETF screeners, automated valuation models, watchlists, real-time market data, and read-only portfolio insights through brokerage connections. It fits users comparing AI investing apps, AI stock screeners, portfolio analysis, and AI-assisted valuation tools. Treat its AI output as a research starting point that needs verification, and treat brokerage integrations as read-only portfolio context rather than trade execution.

tools.name: CapEdge
tools.summary: CapEdge is a free SEC filings, transcripts, IPO, ownership, ETF exposure, and short-interest research platform from Finsight for US equity-capital-markets work. It is strongest for investors who want a registered, no-cost workflow around EDGAR search, filing diffs, filing alerts, XBRL financial charts, holdings, and IPO calendars without paying for a filings terminal.

tools.name: Monexa
tools.summary: Monexa was cataloged as a low-cost AI stock-analysis workspace for screening, company dashboards, financial statements, DCF models, filings, transcripts, ownership views, and congressional-trading research. Its canonical vendor URL returned HTTP 404 when checked on 2026-08-04, and no authoritative successor could be verified. The recorded capabilities and prices are therefore historical context, not confirmation that the service remains available.

tools.name: SentiSense
tools.summary: SentiSense is a beta AI market-intelligence and data API platform for investors and developers who want stock data, sentiment, news clustering, social signals, institutional flows, insider trades, congressional trading disclosures, and AI-generated insights in one workflow. It serves as a signal layer for research, not as a broker or adviser.

tools.name: Options Profit Calculator
tools.summary: Options Profit Calculator is a free web toolkit for modeling option payoff diagrams, profit/loss tables, multi-leg strategies, probability estimates, and what-if scenarios before placing trades elsewhere. Premium beta adds advanced calculators, custom strategies, comparison tools, an options backtester, and ad-free use. It is not a broker, real-time trading terminal, options advisory service, or substitute for risk management.

tools.name: Fintool
tools.summary: Fintool was an AI financial research platform for asking cited questions across SEC filings, earnings transcripts, financial data, screeners, watchlists, and research workflows. It is an acquired legacy product rather than a live self-serve subscription: the public domain redirects to an April 2026 founder update announcing Microsoft acquired Fintool, with the team and IP moving toward Microsoft 365 and Office workflows. Historical context covers the former AI research-agent workflow, not current standalone pricing or signup.

tools.name: Tegus
tools.summary: Tegus is now part of AlphaSense, combining expert-call transcripts, custom expert interviews, financial models, company filings, benchmarking dashboards, Excel workflows, and AI synthesis for professional investment research teams. It supports deep diligence, channel checks, filings, models, and transcript synthesis rather than casual stock screening. Access is custom or enterprise-priced through AlphaSense, with BamSEC Pro still listed separately for filings workflows.

tools.name: Variant
tools.summary: Variant is an AI investment-avatar platform for advanced investors who want to build hedge-fund-style avatars, access continuous market analysis, surface public-market insights, and participate in a tokenized creator/community workflow. Its current focus is investment avatars and AI market analysis rather than the older catalyst-finder positioning. Public pricing is not transparent. It is not a broker, public stock screener, portfolio tracker, licensed adviser, or proof that generated avatar research will be right.

tools.name: OpenCorporates
tools.summary: OpenCorporates is a large legal-entity and company registry database for researchers, investigators, data teams, KYC workflows, ownership mapping, and corporate transparency work. It provides entity identity, provenance, registry links, officer records, relationships, and bulk data rather than stock-market analytics. Free and open-data access is license-limited, while commercial API and bulk SFTP datasets require paid plans. It is not a valuation platform, market-data feed, company fundamentals terminal, broker, or portfolio research product.

tools.name: Social Blade
tools.summary: Social Blade is a social-channel analytics site and API for tracking public creator statistics across YouTube, TikTok, Twitch, Instagram, Facebook, and X/Twitter. It has large branded and YouTube analytics demand, making it useful as alternative data for creator-economy, media, advertising, influencer, and platform research. Free profiles are useful for quick checks, while Premium and Business API tiers expand history, favorites, top lists, report cards, exports, and API credits. It is not a source of private platform data, company fundamentals, portfolio analytics, broker execution, or investment recommendations.

tools.name: Special Situation Investments (SSI)
tools.summary: Special Situation Investments is a niche event-driven research site and paid community for investors looking for special-situation ideas, active discussions, high-conviction writeups, catalyst timelines, upside targets, and member commentary. It is not a broad stock screener, diversified portfolio tool, broker, public API, or recommendation service for every investor.

tools.name: Special Situations Digest
tools.summary: Special Situations Digest is a weekly global event-driven research workflow for investors sourcing activist campaigns, strategic reviews, spin-offs, going-private deals, divestitures, tender offers, restructurings, and M&A across 30+ countries. It is built for fast idea generation and triage, with structured situation cards, a searchable database, spreadsheet/PDF/JSON exports, Copy-for-LLM, and a real-time EDGAR/OTC live feed. It is not a full diligence replacement, valuation modeler, broker, or personalized investment-advice service.

tools.name: PCAOB AuditorSearch
tools.summary: PCAOB AuditorSearch is the official free lookup for the audit firms and engagement partners behind U.S. public-company audit reports. It is useful when governance, audit-quality, restatement, or auditor-change work needs source-level audit provenance rather than another market-data estimate.

tools.name: Trefis
tools.summary: Trefis gives investors interactive, driver-based stock valuation models that show how business assumptions can move an estimated share price. It is strongest for explainable scenario work and public company pages, with paid software positioned around turning model logic into shareable what-if dashboards.

tools.name: Frost & Sullivan
tools.summary: Frost & Sullivan is a premium analyst research, market intelligence, and benchmarking provider for strategy, corporate development, product, and investment teams that need industry reports, Frost Radar studies, economic trackers, growth-opportunity frameworks, and analyst access. It is strongest when the research question is market structure, competitive positioning, technology adoption, or growth opportunity rather than ticker-level fundamentals. Expect consulting-style pricing and sales-led workflows: single reports and enterprise programs can be valuable, but this is not a self-serve investing terminal or open data API.

tools.name: Euromonitor (Passport)
tools.summary: Euromonitor Passport is a premium market-research database for industries, economies, consumers, countries, channels, forecasts, reports, and structured APIs. It is useful when strategy or investment research needs global consumer and industry context beyond public-company filings.

tools.name: IBISWorld
tools.summary: IBISWorld is a premium industry research platform for analysts, lenders, consultants, operators, and investors who need industry reports, risk ratings, forecasts, benchmarking, business environment profiles, API delivery, and AI-assisted report exploration. It is strongest for understanding markets and industries before underwriting a company, sector, customer base, loan, or strategic plan. It is not a stock-analysis terminal: memberships, API access, dashboards, Snowflake delivery, and add-ons are sales-led, while single reports are high-value one-off purchases.

tools.name: AlphaSense
tools.summary: AlphaSense is an enterprise market-intelligence and AI search platform for institutional research, corporate strategy, consulting, investor relations, and buy-side teams that need cited search across broker research, expert transcripts, filings, news, financial data, and internal documents. It is strongest for team-scale research workflows and proprietary content access, with sales-led annual pricing and Enterprise-only internal-content ingestion.

tools.name: Qfinr
tools.summary: Qfinr is a subscription portfolio analytics platform for investors who want multi-asset tracking, risk views, stress testing, and idea discovery without relying on live broker sync. Its public positioning is strongest around portfolio analytics software for Indian and global holdings, with pricing and API details still gated.

tools.name: ORTEX
tools.summary: ORTEX is a market-data and analytics platform best known for short interest, securities lending, options flow, and trading-signal context. It fits active investors, analysts, and data teams that need more than a basic quote page, with deeper web-app and API access moving behind paid tiers.

tools.name: ValuePickr Forum
tools.summary: ValuePickr Forum is a free, India-focused investing community for reading long-form discussions on mid- and small-cap companies. It is useful for qualitative idea discovery and fieldwork-style debate, but posts are community content, reading is not a recommendation, and posting access is invite/manual-screening based.

tools.name: roic.ai
tools.summary: roic.ai is a fundamentals and earnings call transcripts API for developers, quants and AI agents who need financial statements, 90+ pre-calculated ratios (ROIC, ROE, margins) and transcripts for 68k+ companies over REST or MCP, with a free tier of 5 requests per minute.

tools.name: Tijori Finance - Ideas Dashboard
tools.summary: Tijori Finance - Ideas Dashboard is an India-focused stock-idea and market-monitoring workspace built around curated event, fundamental, and operational-data signals. It can surface research leads quickly, but the deeper workflow is Premium-gated and the ideas still need independent verification.

tools.name: Earnings Hub
tools.summary: Earnings Hub is a web and mobile earnings-season workspace for calendars, call access, transcripts, AI summaries, filing summaries, alerts, estimates, and watchlist monitoring. It is useful when your workflow starts with upcoming reports and earnings calls rather than broad valuation screens.

tools.name: Fiscal.ai
tools.summary: Fiscal.ai is an AI-assisted public-company research terminal and financial data API platform for investors, analysts, developers, and AI-agent builders. It combines global fundamentals, segments and KPIs, transcripts, filings, estimates, dashboards, screeners, valuation workflows, AI Copilot, REST APIs, webhooks, and MCP access.

tools.name: GeminIQ
tools.summary: GeminIQ is a browser-based U.S. public-company research platform built around as-filed SEC financial statements. It combines XBRL-traceable 10-K and 10-Q data with calculated metrics, interactive visualizations, reusable custom tables, stock screening, watchlists and comparable-company analysis, Form 4 insider transactions, institutional ownership monitoring, and post-earnings price-reaction views. It is strongest for filing-grounded fundamental research, but coverage is U.S.-focused and new filing data is available the next day rather than in real time.

tools.name: Finatic
tools.summary: Finatic is a broker-connectivity API for fintech builders who need user brokerage linking, normalized brokerage account data, webhooks, and consented trade execution across many brokers. It is useful infrastructure for portfolio apps, trading journals, automation products, copy-trading workflows, and AI/data systems, but it should be evaluated as an early-stage provider with meaningful security, compliance, and broker-specific permission due diligence.

tools.name: Danelfin
tools.summary: Danelfin is an AI stock and ETF scoring platform built around a 1-10 AI Score that estimates the probability of outperforming the market over the next three months. It serves as a ranking, screening, portfolio-alert, and API layer for idea generation, not as a standalone investment process.

tools.name: Lightyear
tools.summary: Lightyear is a low-cost UK and European investing app for stocks, ETFs, funds, bonds, crypto, ready-made plans, multi-currency cash, and light AI-assisted investing workflows. It is useful when brokerage execution and transparent fees matter, but it is not a full equity research terminal, custom factor screener, or backtesting platform.

tools.name: LIQN
tools.summary: LIQN (Liquidation Nation) is a factor-first market intelligence workspace for reading which themes and behaviors are working across 5,000+ stocks, what regime surrounds them, and what may move them next. Its unusual mix spans live factor maps, classified net/gross flows, short-interest context, historical analysis, crowd and podcast intelligence, factor news, event-to-factor exposure mapping, thesis prompts, and custom baskets.

tools.name: AlphaResearch
tools.summary: AlphaResearch is an AI-powered stock research platform for searching filings, transcripts, press releases, reports, notes, fundamentals, estimates, news, insider transactions, institutional ownership, and fund holdings. It is useful for document-heavy research and collaboration, but global coverage and spreadsheet add-ins are Enterprise features and the premium trial requires a credit card.

tools.name: StockInsights.ai
tools.summary: StockInsights.ai is an AI equity research assistant for filings, earnings calls, transcript summaries, 8-K categorization, SEC filing dashboards, watchlist alerts, APIs, and custom research workflows. It is useful for AI-assisted public-company monitoring, but API commercial use, redistribution, higher limits, and custom workflows require separate plans or contact.

tools.name: MoatMap
tools.summary: MoatMap is an AI stock screening and equity research tool with Quality, Value, and Momentum scoring, AI deep dives, insider-trade tracking, portfolio X-Ray, macro regime context, AI Top Picks, and investor-lens checks. It is attractive for fast idea validation and pay-as-you-go research, but premium usage depends on Feather credits and AI outputs still require investor review.

tools.name: WallStreetZen
tools.summary: WallStreetZen is a stock research and screening platform built around Zen Ratings, top analyst tracking, due diligence checks, forecasts, advanced screeners, price-move explanations, and watchlist updates. It fits individual investors who want plain-English research and quant-style grades, but it is US-stock focused and Premium-gated for the strongest ranking and analyst features.

tools.name: Validea
tools.summary: Validea is a factor and guru-strategy research site with stock and ETF model portfolios, guru analysis, factor reports, stock and ETF screeners, trend following, market valuation, portfolio correlation, strategy/ETF matching, alerts, videos, and newsletters. It is useful for systematic idea generation, but model returns are not actual trading results and paid plan pricing is not cleanly published on the reviewed pages.

tools.name: Chaikin Analytics
tools.summary: Chaikin Analytics is a Power Gauge-centered investment research platform with stock and ETF ratings, market insights, newsletters, model portfolios, tactical publications, money-flow ideas, and research products. It is useful for investors who want a blend of fundamental, technical, and money-flow signals, but pricing and entitlements vary by publication and are not summarized in a simple public table.

tools.name: Visual Capitalist
tools.summary: Visual Capitalist is a publisher of data-rich infographics and explainers covering markets, commodities, technology, macroeconomics, and global business themes. It is strongest as visual context for research and presentations, not as a queryable market-data terminal or investment-advice product.

tools.name: Earnings Whispers
tools.summary: Earnings Whispers is an earnings-event research site built around whisper expectations, earnings calendars, sentiment, grades, options context, and post-earnings drift signals. It serves as a setup and expectations tool around earnings, not as a guarantee that a stock will move a certain way.

tools.name: Insider Screener
tools.summary: Insider Screener is a global insider-trading research platform for investors who want to screen, track, export, and alert on director and insider transactions across multiple markets. It is more structured than a simple Form 4 list because it standardizes activity across jurisdictions, supports saved screens and tracked stocks on paid plans, and offers a separate REST API for insider transaction data. It serves as an insider-activity signal layer, not as a complete investment thesis, broker, portfolio accounting system, or unrestricted bulk-data feed.

tools.name: Investment Masters Class (MastersInvest.com)
tools.summary: Investment Masters Class is a free educational site focused on timeless investing lessons, curated reading, investor letters, and essays about great investors and business builders. It is useful for improving process and judgment, not for stock screens, market data, trade signals, or personalized financial advice.

tools.name: Corner of Berkshire & Fairfax (COBF)
tools.summary: Corner of Berkshire & Fairfax is a long-running value-investing forum built around Berkshire, Fairfax, stock ideas, books, and long-form investor discussion. Public boards are useful for idea discovery, while deeper rooms and participation sit behind a one-time lifetime membership.

tools.name: The Earnings Watcher
tools.summary: The Earnings Watcher is a lightweight earnings-alert service for U.S.-listed stocks, with paid Pro access adding broader 6 Signals history and trend views. It is best for keeping earnings events and basic company-quality signals visible, not for replacing a brokerage platform or full options-risk workflow.

tools.name: The Ledger Terminal
tools.summary: The Ledger Terminal is a web-based fundamental stock research terminal built around one-page U.S. stock tearsheets, valuation charts, quality checks, screeners, comparisons, and SEC-linked financial history. It is aimed at long-term business analysis, not trading execution or portfolio accounting.

tools.name: FT Markets (Markets data - Financial Times)
tools.summary: FT Markets is the Financial Times market-data portal for global equities, funds, ETFs, bonds, commodities, currencies, watchlists, portfolios, alerts, charts, and screeners. It is useful for readers who want credible market tools close to the FT news workflow rather than a standalone professional terminal. Free registration unlocks practical tracking tools, but deeper company data, director dealings, archive PDFs, and parts of the broader FT experience can require a subscription, and market data is delayed.

tools.name: 10X EBITDA - Hedge Fund Presentations
tools.summary: 10X EBITDA - Hedge Fund Presentations is a free archive of value-investing, activist, and hedge-fund pitch decks for people who want to study how professional investors build stock theses. It is best treated as an educational idea and case-study library, not as a live market-data product, screener, portfolio tool, or source of current investment recommendations.

tools.name: Tracefour
tools.summary: Tracefour is a free insider-trade heatmap for investors who want to scan U.S. insider filings, selected European director-dealing disclosures, and U.S. Congress trades in one browser view. It is useful when OpenInsider's U.S.-only Form 4 scope is too narrow, but it should be treated as a discovery layer rather than an institutional data feed because public pages do not publish an API, export workflow, commercial SLA, or data-license terms.

tools.name: OpenInsider
tools.summary: OpenInsider is a free, utilitarian SEC Form 4 insider-trading screener for investors who want to monitor insider buying, insider selling, cluster buys, and transaction reports without paying for a data terminal. It is useful for fast first-pass insider activity research, but the interface is table-heavy and there is no formal paid support, SLA, mobile app, or documented public API.

tools.name: Oilprice.com
tools.summary: Oilprice.com is an energy-market news and data hub for oil prices, crude blends, rig counts, commodity context, and energy-sector analysis. It is useful for macro and commodity monitoring, while premium access is newsletter-style research rather than a full trading or data terminal.

tools.name: Statfolio
tools.summary: Statfolio is a lightweight stock and ETF portfolio tracker for investors who want holdings, performance, dividends, splits, diversification, and symbol research in one dashboard. It fits manual or imported tracking workflows, not brokerage execution or a full research terminal.

tools.name: Stock Unlock
tools.summary: Stock Unlock is a global stock and ETF research platform that combines stock scores, screeners, DCF tools, comparison charts, watchlists, and portfolio tracking. It is built for retail investors who want research and portfolio context together, with deeper history and broker links moving behind paid plans.

tools.name: Stockoscope
tools.summary: Stockoscope is a visual U.S. stock research platform built around five connected lenses: quality, peers, valuation, analysts, and holdings. It combines configurable fundamental scores, peer ranks, intrinsic-value models, analyst estimates, ownership activity, screeners, editable investment strategies, watchlists, and news. It is approachable for retail investors and unusually transparent about its model rules and data sources, but coverage is U.S.-only and data generally refreshes daily or after market close.

tools.name: NerdWallet Compound Interest Calculator
tools.summary: NerdWallet Compound Interest Calculator is a free, no-login calculator for estimating how savings or investments may grow with compound interest. It is best for simple education and scenario planning, not portfolio imports, market data, tax modeling, or investment advice.

tools.name: Track Your Dividends (TYD)
tools.summary: Track Your Dividends is a dividend-focused portfolio tracker for U.S. investors, combining Plaid-linked accounts, manual portfolios, dividend alerts, income projections, and Premium research tools. It is useful for dividend monitoring, but deeper screening, scores, analysis, and unlimited linked accounts are paid.

tools.name: PortfoliosLab
tools.summary: PortfoliosLab is a web-based portfolio analytics platform for backtesting, optimization, risk metrics, correlations, screeners, and AI-assisted portfolio workflows. It is useful for comparing stocks, ETFs, funds, crypto, and model portfolios, with more history, imports, exports, and MCP access gated by paid tiers.

tools.name: ETF Research Center
tools.summary: ETF Research Center is an ETF analytics site powered by AltaVista Research, focused on constituent fundamentals, valuations, overlap, stock locator workflows, portfolio building, and ETF reports. It is useful when ETF analysis needs to look through the fund wrapper into holdings and fundamental exposure.

tools.name: Finimize
tools.summary: Finimize is a consumer investing newsletter and mobile app for investors who want concise market news, investing education, analyst-backed ideas, model portfolios, and an easier daily research habit. It is strongest when the goal is understanding what matters in markets without opening a data terminal: the free newsletter covers short daily finance news, while Pro adds investment theses, entry points, risks, position sizing, ongoing coverage, live ideas, model portfolios, and performance tracking. It is a content and ideas product, not a broker, portfolio accounting tool, public API, or deep analytics platform.

tools.name: Bridgewater Associates
tools.summary: Bridgewater Associates is a global macro investment manager whose public website is mainly useful as a free research and insights source, not as a self-serve investing product. It is strongest for readers studying institutional macro thinking, Daily Observations, whitepapers, videos, Pure Alpha, All Weather, risk parity, inflation, monetary policy, debt cycles, and systematic investing, but most investors cannot directly access Bridgewater mandates through the site.

tools.name: eToro
tools.summary: eToro is a multi-asset broker and social trading platform for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, commodities, and currencies where available. It is useful when CopyTrader, Smart Portfolios, fractional investing, and a large demo account matter more than advanced research or tax-lot workflows.

tools.name: Markets.com
tools.summary: Markets.com is a global CFD broker for traders who want web, mobile, desktop, MetaTrader, TradingView, and social/copy-trading access across forex, shares, commodities, indices, ETFs, bonds, and crypto CFDs where permitted. It is an execution platform rather than a research-only tool, so product availability, leverage, protections, and costs depend heavily on jurisdiction. A free account does not make trading free: spreads, swaps, currency conversion, taxes, and other account charges can still matter.

tools.name: Quartr
tools.summary: Quartr is a qualitative public-market research platform for earnings calls, real-time transcripts, filings, reports, slide decks, analyst estimates, AI chat, and investor-relations data. The mobile app is useful for free earnings-call and transcript access, while Quartr Pro and Quartr API serve professional research, MCP, webhook, and data-integration workflows.

tools.name: ETF.com
tools.summary: ETF.com is an ETF media and research site with a U.S. ETF screener, comparison tools, fund flows, holdings search, watchlists, Portfolio Builder, launches, closures, and ETF education. It is useful when you want ETF discovery plus editorial context from a known ETF-focused brand.

tools.name: Trendlyne
tools.summary: Trendlyne is an India-first equity research and portfolio platform with screeners, DVM scores, analyst forecasts, alerts, backtests, transcripts, broker sync, and options tools. Global plans add U.S. market coverage, but the strongest fit is still Indian market research with tiered data downloads and alert limits.

tools.name: IPOScoop
tools.summary: IPOScoop is a U.S. IPO calendar, pricing, ratings, and IPO news site for investors who follow new issues from filing through pricing, first-day trading, quiet-period expiration, and lock-up expiration. Free pages cover IPO calendars, recent pricings, recent IPO lists, and IPO Buzz commentary, while subscriber access unlocks SCOOP Ratings and selected event trackers. It supports U.S. IPO monitoring, not as a broad stock screener, broker, valuation platform, or investment-advice service.

tools.name: ChartMill
tools.summary: ChartMill is a browser-based stock screener, charting, ratings, alerts, and research platform for self-directed traders and investors screening U.S., Canadian, and European stocks and some ETFs. It is strongest for repeatable technical and fundamental screen workflows, swing-trading ideas, watchlists, alerts, market dashboards, ChartMill ratings, and strategy templates, but paid access does not turn it into a real-time broker or full portfolio accounting system.

tools.name: ETFdb ETF Screener
tools.summary: ETFdb ETF Screener is a VettaFi ETF database and screener for U.S.-listed ETFs and ETPs, with filters for returns, flows, expenses, ESG, dividends, risk, holdings, taxes, technicals, and ratings. It is useful when ETF selection needs structured screening and exportable results.

tools.name: Revolut (Invest)
tools.summary: Revolut Invest is the investing surface inside Revolut’s broader money app, built for eligible users who want simple mobile access to stocks, ETFs/ETPs, bonds, crypto, commodities, alerts, news, and basic portfolio tracking. It is strongest for existing Revolut customers and beginner-friendly investing, but fees, asset availability, Trading Pro, crypto, commodities, and robo-advisor access vary heavily by country, entity, and plan.

tools.name: Wise (Interest & Stocks)
tools.summary: Wise Interest and Stocks are account features for eligible Wise customers who want interest-like balance options or simple one-fund stock exposure inside a multi-currency account. Availability, fees, insurance treatment, fund choice, and settlement behavior vary by country, so it should not be presented as a full brokerage.

tools.name: N26
tools.summary: N26 Invest brings stocks, ETFs, crypto, ready-made funds, and recurring plans into the N26 mobile banking app where those products are available. It is built for convenient bank-native investing in eligible European markets, not advanced research, web trading, or developer data access.

tools.name: Scalable Capital
tools.summary: Scalable Capital is a European broker and wealth platform for stocks, ETFs, funds, bonds, crypto ETPs, derivatives, savings plans, and automated ETF portfolios. It is strongest for eligible EU investors who want low-cost recurring investing and simple web/mobile execution, not a public API or research terminal.

tools.name: Cash App
tools.summary: Cash App Investing is a U.S.-only beginner brokerage inside Cash App for users who want simple stock, ETF, and Bitcoin access, fractional shares, recurring buys, Round Ups, tax forms, and low-friction investing from a mobile payments app. It is strongest for small-dollar beginners who value convenience, but it lacks advanced research, options, bonds, portfolio analytics, broad order types, and global availability.

tools.name: Macrotrends
tools.summary: Macrotrends is a web-based historical charting, stock research, and macro data site for investors who want long-run stock prices, fundamentals, dividends, indices, commodities, exchange rates, interest rates, global metrics, and a simple stock screener. It is useful for quick visual context and historical series, especially when users need low-friction charts rather than a full research terminal. Some data, charts, downloads, or resources require Premium Access, with pricing shown at checkout and no monthly billing recorded in the current terms.

tools.name: justETF
tools.summary: justETF is a Europe-first ETF research, comparison, and portfolio-planning platform for investors building UCITS ETF and ETC portfolios. It combines ETF screening, fund profiles, stock-to-ETF exposure lookup, watchlists, transaction-based portfolios, savings-plan workflows, simulations, rebalancing, attribution, and mobile alerts. It is strongest for European ETF investors, not U.S.-listed ETF workflows, broker execution, tax-lot accounting, or public API access.

tools.name: The Zen of Investing
tools.summary: The Zen of Investing is a free, niche special-situations site focused on upcoming and recent spinoffs. It is useful for event-driven investors who want curated links to press releases, investor decks, prospectuses, filings, and SEC feeds before doing deeper valuation work elsewhere.

tools.name: WhaleWisdom
tools.summary: WhaleWisdom is a 13F, institutional ownership, insider, and hedge-fund holdings platform for investors who track filer activity, fund portfolios, watchlists, backtests, exports, and API workflows. It is useful for holdings research, but 13F data is delayed and the deeper history/API workflow is paid.

tools.name: ConsumerAffairs
tools.summary: ConsumerAffairs is a consumer-review and buyer-guide site that can help investors and operators read reputation, complaint, and product-experience signals around consumer-facing companies. It serves as qualitative alternative data for brand and customer-risk research, with care around review sampling and commercial placement.

tools.name: okama
tools.summary: okama is a free open-source portfolio analytics toolkit with web widgets, a REST API, and a Python library for efficient frontiers, risk metrics, Monte Carlo simulations, cash-flow modeling, and historical market or macro data. It is best for technical users who want reproducible analysis rather than a consumer portfolio tracker.

tools.name: Glassdoor
tools.summary: Glassdoor is an employee reviews, salary, jobs, and employer-branding platform that investors can use as alternative context on culture, hiring, retention, compensation pressure, employer reputation, and workforce sentiment. It is strongest for qualitative diligence around companies where people, recruiting, or labor costs matter, not for market data or financial modeling. Treat Glassdoor signals as noisy, self-selected, and supporting evidence: they can flag questions for deeper work, but they do not replace filings, fundamentals, interviews, or primary company analysis.

tools.name: MSN Money
tools.summary: MSN Money is a free, ad-supported Microsoft finance portal for market news, stock quotes, watchlists, company pages, earnings calendars, funds, and basic personal-finance tools. It is built for casual monitoring and beginner research, not professional analytics, brokerage execution, or advisory workflows.

tools.name: Asset Allocation Interactive (AAI)
tools.summary: Asset Allocation Interactive is Research Affiliates’ free capital-market-expectations and portfolio-construction tool for investors, advisors, and analysts comparing long-term expected returns across asset classes. It is strongest for strategic allocation work and model-portfolio scenarios, not for security selection, brokerage execution, tax tracking, or real-time portfolio monitoring.

tools.name: MarketInOut
tools.summary: MarketInOut is a formula-driven stock, ETF, forex, and crypto screener with historical screening, strategy backtesting, alerts, watchlists, simple portfolio views, correlation tools, and one-time membership terms. It fits traders who want custom screening rules and backtests without a recurring monthly SaaS subscription. Free access is limited, serious workflows are paid, and it does not provide broker execution, broker sync, or automated trading.

tools.name: MarketSurge
tools.summary: MarketSurge is Investor’s Business Daily’s premium stock research, screening, charting, ratings, alerts, and idea-list platform for IBD-style growth and swing traders. It carries the MarketSmith lineage and emphasizes pattern recognition, buy zones, sell signals, IBD ratings, curated growth lists, earnings lines, forward estimates, institutional demand, and Dow Jones news. It is expensive and methodology-specific, so it fits users committed to IBD/CANSLIM workflows better than casual investors or users seeking broker execution, tax-aware portfolio tracking, or broad factor research.

tools.name: Marketgenius
tools.summary: Marketgenius is a free, mobile-friendly stock heatmap and lightweight stock dashboard site for quick visual discovery. It focuses on major U.S. index heatmaps, superinvestor portfolio heatmaps, simple stock fundamentals, ownership stats, valuation metrics, dividend details, short interest, and basic scores. It serves as a fast visual starting point, not as a full screener, deep financial terminal, broker, API, or valuation platform.

tools.name: Marketlog
tools.summary: Marketlog is a web and mobile portfolio tracker for retail investors and active traders who want manual or broker-connected portfolios, dividend tracking, goals, target allocation, benchmarking, forecasts, alerts, market pages, calendars, and public or private portfolio sharing. It is useful for monitoring holdings and portfolio behavior across asset types, especially when users want mobile access and community portfolio browsing. It is not a broker, exchange, fiduciary, investment adviser, or public market-data API.

tools.name: European Central Bank (ECB) — Statistics & Data
tools.summary: European Central Bank Statistics & Data is the official ECB source for euro-area statistics, policy rates, FX reference rates, yield curves, inflation, macro indicators, downloads, and SDMX API access. It is useful when you need primary-source European macro and rates data rather than investment-app commentary.

tools.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
tools.summary: The Bank of Japan website is the official free source for Japanese monetary policy releases, meeting schedules, BOJ statistics, release calendars, time-series downloads, charts, and API access. It is strongest for analysts, students, developers, and investors who need primary-source Japan rates, FX, money stock, TANKAN, balance-of-payments, and central-bank data, but it is a macro data source rather than an investing app or security-level research terminal.

tools.name: Bank of England
tools.summary: The Bank of England website is the official free source for UK monetary policy decisions, Bank Rate context, MPC calendars and minutes, Monetary Policy Reports, statistics, exchange-rate and interest-rate series, and UK yield-curve downloads. It is strongest as a primary-source macro and rates reference for analysts, students, investors, and developers, but it is not an investing app and some datasets, including yield curves, are delivered as files rather than a full API.

tools.name: Federal Reserve Board (FRB.gov)
tools.summary: Federal Reserve Board (FRB.gov) is the official U.S. central-bank source for policy materials, FOMC calendars, statistical releases, interest rates, balance sheet data, bank data, FX rates, industrial production, and Data Download Program files. It serves as a primary macro source, not a commercial investing terminal.

tools.name: NYSE (Exchange Data & Tech)
tools.summary: NYSE Data & Tech is primary exchange-data infrastructure for institutions, vendors, and developers that need licensed U.S. equities, options, bonds, real-time feeds, historical TAQ, reference data, and corporate actions. It is authoritative data plumbing, not a retail research app.

tools.name: ICE Index Platform (ICE Data Indices)
tools.summary: ICE Index Platform is an enterprise index-data platform for institutional users who need licensed ICE index levels, constituent statistics, historical performance, fixed-income benchmarks, automated feeds, custom index tools, and the ICE Global Index Feed. It is strongest for benchmark, risk, product, and data teams working with official ICE index families rather than retail investors looking for simple charts. Access is governed by trial review, subscriptions, licensing, and data-usage restrictions; it is not a free public benchmark database.

tools.name: Koyfin
tools.summary: Koyfin is a modern web and mobile financial terminal for investors, analysts, and advisors who want dashboards, charts, screeners, portfolios, news, alerts, transcripts, and market data without using a traditional desktop terminal. It is strongest for building custom research workspaces across equities, ETFs, funds, macro data, FX, commodities, crypto, yield curves, and advisor reporting. Free access is useful for trialing the workflow, while paid and Advisor tiers unlock more dashboards, screens, history, alerts, reporting, integrations, and client-portfolio features. It does not offer a public API.

tools.name: Benzinga
tools.summary: Benzinga is a market-news, trading-tools, and financial-data platform for active traders, investors, developers, and data buyers who need fast news, alerts, scanners, calendars, squawk, options activity, analyst actions, filings, transcripts, and APIs. It is strongest for event-driven monitoring and real-time workflow around Benzinga Pro or licensed feeds, but the useful trading features are paid, tiered, or add-on based, and the product is not a long-term portfolio accounting system.

tools.name: Berkshire Hathaway Archive (Memorex)
tools.summary: Berkshire Hathaway Archive by Memorex is a free searchable document archive for Warren Buffett shareholder letters and Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting transcripts. It is strongest for value investors, students, and researchers who want semantic search across Berkshire source material on capital allocation, incentives, moats, management, insurance, and long-term investing, but it is a single-company archive rather than a market-data product or general transcript database.

tools.name: The Wall Street Journal (WSJ)
tools.summary: The Wall Street Journal combines premium business journalism with a Market Data Center for quotes, calendars, company pages, analyst estimates, ratings, dividends, and market statistics. It is best for news-led market context, with much of the value behind a WSJ subscription and market data subject to exchange delays.

tools.name: Bloomberg (Europe)
tools.summary: Bloomberg Europe is the Bloomberg.com regional news hub and mobile-app experience for readers who want global business journalism, European market coverage, market snapshots, watchlists, alerts, Bloomberg TV and radio, podcasts, newsletters, and Bloomberg Businessweek access. It is strongest as a premium media subscription for investors and analysts, but it is not Bloomberg Terminal and does not provide professional terminal entitlements, execution, or institutional data workflows.

tools.name: Barron's
tools.summary: Barron's is a subscription investing publication from Dow Jones for investors who want market journalism, stock ideas, portfolio context, newsletters, mobile access, and a Market Data Center for quotes, screeners, funds, bonds, commodities, currencies, and crypto. It is strongest for editorial analysis and investor reading workflows, while pricing is promotion-heavy, premium products can be separate upsells, and it is not a modeling terminal, broker, or public data API.

tools.name: QuantRocket
tools.summary: QuantRocket is a Docker- and Jupyter-based quant research, backtesting, data, and live-trading platform for technical Python users. It is strongest when you want local infrastructure, Interactive Brokers integration, point-in-time research, and API/CLI workflows rather than a point-and-click retail app.

tools.name: QuantConnect
tools.summary: QuantConnect is an algorithmic trading platform built on the open-source LEAN engine, connecting research, backtesting, cloud deployment, broker integrations, and live trading. It is built for technical Python or C# users who want multi-asset systematic trading infrastructure, not a simple retail charting app.

tools.name: BankAnalysis
tools.summary: BankAnalysis is a private-beta research platform built specifically for U.S. bank stocks, combining standardized bank financials, bank-specific metrics, SEC filings, earnings-call transcripts, screening, peer comparison, charts, branch maps, and a cited AI analyst named Jamie. It is strongest for investors and analysts who need deposits, net interest margin, credit quality, capital, branches, and regulatory-style bank context instead of generic equity metrics, but access is still waitlist/private beta and public pricing is not posted.

tools.name: Business Quant
tools.summary: Business Quant is a U.S. equities research, screening, KPI, and financial-data platform for investors who want fundamentals, operating metrics, segment data, analyst estimates, ratings, warnings, 13F ownership, insider trades, exports, and API access. It is strongest for U.S. stock research where business-driver KPIs matter, but free KPI depth is shallow and serious API, export, history, and commercial-use workflows require paid plans.

tools.name: Autochartist
tools.summary: Autochartist is an automated market-scanning and trader-engagement platform for active traders, brokers, and trading platforms that want chart-pattern detection, technical trade setups, economic-event analysis, news sentiment, alerts, position sizing, and API or MetaTrader integrations. It is strongest as a signal and workflow layer around technical trading, but pricing, modules, and access often depend on a broker or enterprise relationship rather than a simple public checkout.

tools.name: Firefly III
tools.summary: Firefly III is a free, open-source, self-hosted personal finance manager for people who want control over their own budgeting, accounts, transactions, categories, tags, reports, imports, API access, and automation. It belongs in investing-tool comparisons only when the user is looking for personal finance infrastructure, not stock research: it can track money flows and budgets, but it is not a broker, market-data terminal, tax-lot engine, or portfolio analytics platform. The main tradeoff is operational responsibility: users must host it, secure it, back it up, update it, and configure imports themselves.

tools.name: Financial Modeling Prep (FMP)
tools.summary: Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) is a market-data API and spreadsheet-data provider for developers, analysts, quants, and product builders who need equities, ETFs, funds, FX, crypto, commodities, macro, ESG, ownership, news, calendars, transcripts, and fundamentals from one vendor. It is strongest when you want REST and WebSocket access plus Excel and Google Sheets add-ins at a lower entry price than enterprise terminals. The main buying questions are plan limits, geography, history depth, and dataset access: the free Basic tier is a limited EOD sandbox, while real-time, global, transcript, 13F, holdings, intraday, and bulk workflows require paid tiers.

tools.name: FinancialData.Net
tools.summary: FinancialData.Net is an API-first financial data platform for developers, analysts, spreadsheet users, and AI-agent builders who want broad market data, fundamentals, ownership, options, funds, ESG, calendars, news, Excel access, and MCP connectivity from one provider. It is strongest when breadth matters: stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, options, futures, crypto, forex, commodities, OTC securities, indices, filings-related datasets, and institutional/insider activity can sit behind one REST API. Serious use is paid, and compliance/security claims should be verified directly because no public audit reports were identified.

tools.name: EODHD
tools.summary: EODHD is a market-data API provider for developers, quants, and analysts who need REST, WebSocket, spreadsheet, and AI-agent access to historical prices, fundamentals, calendars, news, sentiment, options, forex, crypto, and other financial datasets. It is strongest for API-first data workflows, but free usage is tiny, commercial licensing is separate, and some datasets require add-ons or marketplace plans.

tools.name: Intrinio
tools.summary: Intrinio is a financial data infrastructure vendor for developers, data teams, and AI builders who need licensed market data, fundamentals, options, ETF, mutual-fund, analyst, dividend, split, and company-news datasets through APIs, WebSockets, files, Snowflake, S3, and selected FTP workflows. It is strongest when the buyer needs production data delivery and usage rights rather than an end-user research app. Pricing, entitlements, real-time access, redistribution, and delivery methods vary by dataset and plan, so it should be evaluated as a vendor contract rather than a simple retail subscription.

tools.name: Marketstack
tools.summary: Marketstack is an APILayer REST market-data API for developers who need stock prices, end-of-day history, intraday bars, corporate actions, reference data, ETF holdings, bond yields, commodities, analyst ratings, and SEC EDGAR company datasets through JSON endpoints. It is useful for prototypes and products that need a simple stock market API with a free tier and clear paid plans. It is not a charting app, broker, portfolio tracker, screener UI, or unlimited institutional data license.

tools.name: MesoSim
tools.summary: MesoSim is an options strategy backtesting platform for traders who need low-code strategy definitions, multi-leg simulations, risk graphs, Greeks, volatility surfaces, margin models, and paper/live workflow paths. It is narrow by design: options research first, not broad stock research or portfolio accounting.

tools.name: Tweenvest
tools.summary: Tweenvest is a web-based stock research app with company dashboards, screeners, watchlists, portfolio tracking, transcripts, valuation tools, and AI-assisted analysis. It is positioned for retail investors, especially European and Spain-aware workflows, with the best coverage and AI features reserved for higher tiers.

tools.name: TIKR
tools.summary: TIKR is a browser-based global equity research terminal for investors who care about fundamentals, financial statements, analyst estimates, valuation work, transcripts, filings, and stock screening. It is strongest for long-term stock research across global markets, with paid plans unlocking the deeper history, broader coverage, exports, and workflow limits that serious investors usually need.

tools.name: Reflexivity
tools.summary: Reflexivity is a sales-led institutional AI investment research platform for hedge funds, asset managers, and professional teams that need explainable outputs over trusted market, filing, transcript, portfolio, and scenario data. It is enterprise research infrastructure, not a self-serve retail stock app.

tools.name: Relative Rotation Graphs® (RRG Research)
tools.summary: Relative Rotation Graphs from RRG Research are specialized visual tools for comparing relative strength and rotation across securities, sectors, asset classes, currencies, crypto, or custom professional universes. The low-cost web app is intentionally lightweight, while API and branded implementations are contact-priced professional services.

tools.name: MarineTraffic
tools.summary: MarineTraffic is a global AIS vessel-tracking platform for monitoring ships, voyages, ports, route forecasts, custom areas, alerts, historical tracks, and maritime data APIs. Investors can use it as shipping, commodity, trade, and supply-chain alternative data, especially when vessel movements or port calls matter to a thesis. It is not a securities database, pricing feed, fundamentals product, broker, or portfolio analytics tool, and API access depends on account-specific entitlements.

tools.name: World Bank Open Data (data.worldbank.org)
tools.summary: World Bank Open Data is a free official source for global macroeconomic, development, GDP, population, inflation, trade, and country-level indicators. It is valuable for research, dashboards, and macro context, but it is not security pricing, company fundamentals, portfolio analytics, or real-time market data.

tools.name: Observatory of Economic Complexity (OEC)
tools.summary: The Observatory of Economic Complexity is a trade-data and economic-complexity platform for exploring countries, products, industries, exports, imports, rankings, and trade relationships through rich visualizations and an API. It is useful for macro, supply-chain, and thematic research, not security-level stock analysis.

tools.name: Reuters
tools.summary: Reuters is a global news source with dedicated Markets coverage, company pages, delayed quote data, newsletters, mobile alerts, watchlists, and LSEG-sourced financials and key metrics. It is best for trusted news flow and market context, not advanced research software or a public investor API.

tools.name: SEC API (sec-api.io)
tools.summary: SEC API is a commercial SEC/EDGAR API suite for developers, quants, compliance teams, and AI products that need fast filing search, real-time feeds, XBRL-to-JSON conversion, section extraction, insider filings, 13F data, and other structured regulatory datasets. It is strongest when you want production-ready normalized SEC data instead of building your own EDGAR ingestion stack, but the free tier is only a small starter allowance and redistribution requires enterprise terms.

tools.name: Ghostfolio
tools.summary: Ghostfolio is an open-source, privacy-focused portfolio and wealth tracker for investors who want self-hosted control, multi-account portfolio tracking, net-worth dashboards, imports, charts, risk views, and REST API access. It is strongest for technical users who prefer transparency and self-hosting over a closed portfolio app, with Ghostfolio Premium available for managed cloud hosting and professional data-provider access. The tradeoff is operational: free use requires running and maintaining your own instance, while cloud pricing and data-provider details should be checked before choosing Premium.

tools.name: Tickertape
tools.summary: Tickertape is an India-first investing app for researching stocks, mutual funds, and ETFs, building screeners, tracking portfolios, and connecting broker accounts for a research-to-transaction workflow. It is strongest for Indian retail investors who want stock pages, analyst forecasts, Market Mood Index sentiment, portfolio alerts, corporate events, and broker-linked holdings in one web and mobile product. Free access covers the core experience, while Pro adds custom screens and filters, exports, historical MMI, advanced alerts, forecasts, premium screens, and multi-account portfolio features. It is not a raw market-data API or a full global institutional terminal.

tools.name: OpenBB
tools.summary: OpenBB combines an open-source financial data layer with a hosted Workspace for dashboards, AI research, custom agents, and team workflows. It is best for analysts, quants, developers, and firms that want to connect their own market data, internal datasets, provider API keys, widgets, MCP tools, and AI workflows instead of buying a closed terminal. Community access is useful for individuals; Lite adds a self-hosted collaboration tier without Excel or Copilot, while Pro adds the broader enterprise feature and deployment set. OpenBB does not provide production market data itself; it orchestrates connectors, your data, and your vendor access.

tools.name: Nasdaq.com
tools.summary: Nasdaq.com is Nasdaq's official investor portal for quotes, market news, screeners, calendars, filings, options chains, watchlists, and portfolio tools. It is strongest for investors who want exchange-branded market pages, earnings and dividend calendars, IPO context, ETF and fund screeners, company financials, insider and institutional ownership, and options-chain lookup without buying licensed exchange data products. Smart Portfolio Pro adds TipRanks-powered broker syncing and portfolio analytics. Nasdaq.com is not Nasdaq Data Link, a licensed exchange feed, a broker, or a professional market-data API.

tools.name: Damodaran Online (NYU Stern)
tools.summary: Damodaran Online is Aswath Damodaran's free NYU Stern valuation resource for investors, students, and analysts who need downloadable datasets, valuation models, equity risk premiums, country risk premiums, betas, multiples, and corporate-finance teaching material. It is a trusted manual research library, not a polished stock terminal, screener, alert product, or real-time data feed.

tools.name: Estimize
tools.summary: Estimize is a crowdsourced earnings and macro-estimates platform for investors and data teams that want alternative expectations data before company reports and economic releases. It supports EPS, revenue, and macro forecast context, not for broad portfolio management or trading execution.

tools.name: Stocktwits
tools.summary: Stocktwits is a social investing network for following real-time market conversation, community sentiment, trending symbols, watchlists, earnings context, news, and symbol pages across stocks, ETFs, and crypto. It is strongest when retail attention, sentiment shifts, and fast-moving discussion matter as much as traditional quote pages. Free access covers the core community and market-monitoring experience; Ad Free removes ads, Edge adds social sentiment and expanded market-list data, and enterprise API access is request-based. Treat its posts and sentiment as market context, not verified research or investment advice.

tools.name: Perplexity Finance
