tools.summary: Perplexity Finance is an AI-assisted finance research experience that combines cited answers with stock, ETF, fund, crypto, options, news, charts, screeners, earnings documents, ownership data, government trading views, and a developer finance_search tool. It is strongest for quick cited research and agentic finance data access, but AI answers still need verification and consumer plans are separate from Agent API billing.

tools.name: Zacks (Zacks.com)
tools.summary: Zacks.com is a retail equity and fund research site built around the Zacks Rank, earnings-estimate revisions, Style Scores, screeners, calendars, ETF research, and portfolio alerts. It is strongest for investors who specifically want Zacks' ranking framework, earnings-surprise workflows, analyst estimate context, and long-running premium research services rather than a modern modeling workspace. Free access covers basic research pages and screeners; Premium and higher tiers unlock the full #1 Rank list, Equity Research Reports, Focus List, Earnings ESP, and premium screens. It is not a broker, public API, portfolio accounting system, or licensed data feed.

tools.name: Google Finance
tools.summary: Google Finance is a free market-monitoring hub for investors who want familiar quotes, charts, financial news, watchlists, manual portfolios, earnings context, and AI-assisted research without paying for a terminal. It is best for quick orientation and portfolio/watchlist monitoring, with sign-in required for personal lists, portfolios, and deeper AI Research features.

tools.name: SEC.gov (EDGAR)
tools.summary: SEC.gov EDGAR is the official free source for U.S. public-company filings, fund filings, insider forms, 13F reports, full-text filing search, RSS feeds, bulk archives, and no-key public JSON APIs. It is the baseline source for filings research and data validation, but it is raw official infrastructure rather than a polished commercial research terminal.

tools.name: TradeBB
tools.summary: TradeBB is a web-based trading journal for importing trades, reviewing performance, writing notes, and analyzing behavior across stocks, options, futures, and forex. It is strongest for traders who want a free-start journal with selected broker sync, trade file uploads, dashboard analytics, calendar views, reports, tags, strategies, and notes. Free supports basic review and one active trade dataset; Pro adds advanced analytics, multi-account insights, and professional reporting. TradeBB is not a broker, signal service, or execution platform.

tools.name: TradeZella
tools.summary: TradeZella is a paid trading journal for active traders who want broker imports, performance analytics, tagging, playbooks, backtesting, replay, AI review, risk reports, and mentor workflows in one web platform. It is strongest for traders improving process and execution discipline across stocks, options, forex, futures, and crypto rather than researching long-term investments. Essential, Pro, and Ultra differ by connected-account limits, AI credits, automated AI backtests, and replay depth. TradeZella is not a brokerage.

tools.name: Tradervue
tools.summary: Tradervue is a mature trading journal for importing trades, reviewing charts, analyzing performance, sharing trades, working with mentors, and using reports across stocks, ETFs, futures, forex, and options. It is strongest for active traders who want post-trade analytics, broker sync or file imports, chart-based review, MFE/MAE analysis, R-based risk reporting, CSV exports, and a public REST API. Free access is useful for light journaling but capped at 30 grouped trades per month; Silver and Gold unlock the serious reporting and import workflows. Tradervue is not a broker, tax-lot accounting system, or market-discovery platform.

tools.name: ShortSqueeze.com
tools.summary: ShortSqueeze.com is a members-only U.S. short-interest research service for traders who want screens, rankings, ticker pages, historical short data, and Excel downloads focused on potential short-squeeze setups. It is strongest when the job is narrow: finding stocks with high short interest, days-to-cover, short percent of float, recent short-interest changes, and related technical context. Membership includes rolling history and market-wide data downloads, while older archives and multi-user access are separate. It is not a broad stock research platform, broker, real-time quote terminal, or guarantee that high short interest will lead to a squeeze.

tools.name: FlowAlgo
tools.summary: FlowAlgo is an options-flow and dark-pool monitoring platform for traders who want a focused tape of unusual options activity, sweeps, block trades, equity blocks, dark-pool prints, alerts, and historical flow. It is strongest when the research question is what large or unusual traders may be doing right now, not when you need a broker, fundamentals terminal, options backtester, or portfolio system. The pricing decision matters: there is no free tier, the trial is paid, and flow signals still require interpretation because order flow does not prove intent, direction, or profitability.

tools.name: HighShortInterest.com
tools.summary: HighShortInterest.com is a simple free list of U.S. stocks with short interest above 20%, organized by exchange for users who want a fast starting point for heavily shorted names. It is strongest as a no-login, read-only shortcut for short-interest idea discovery. It is not a full screener or institutional dataset: source detail, methodology, downloads, APIs, alerts, and real-time positioning are not provided, and the site itself tells users to verify the data elsewhere.

tools.name: Short Interest - FMM
tools.summary: Short Interest - FMM is Find My Moat’s free high-short-interest stock tracker for users who want a quick searchable list of U.S. stocks with short interest above 20%. It is strongest for first-pass short-interest and short-squeeze discovery inside Find My Moat, with a sortable table and plain-English education, but it depends on an upstream source and is not a trade signal, export feed, or API.

tools.name: Stockcircle
tools.summary: Stockcircle is a web app for following disclosed investor portfolios, guru transactions, insider trades, U.S. Congress trades, ETF holdings, valuation pages, screeners, alerts, and Pro-only AI earnings-call summaries. It is strongest for retail investors who want idea generation from reported holdings and public transaction disclosures without manually combing through filings. Pro unlocks fuller history, full screener access, instant notifications, stock picks, ad-free use, and AI summaries. The data is useful but inherently incomplete because SEC reporting rules do not require every holding or smaller transaction to be disclosed.

tools.name: StockCharts
tools.summary: StockCharts is a long-running browser-based charting, scanning, alerting, and technical-analysis platform for traders and investors who organize work around charts, ChartLists, scans, alerts, RRGs, PerfCharts, options tools, and saved layouts. It is strongest for technical workflows rather than fundamental modeling or portfolio accounting. Free access and BATS real-time quotes are useful starting points, while Basic, Extra, and PRO expand chart history, scans, alerts, ChartLists, refresh rates, layouts, exports, and data depth. Real-time exchange data, OptionsPlay, and some trading workflows require add-ons or linked services.

tools.name: TC2000
tools.summary: TC2000 is a long-standing charting, scanning, alerting, paper-trading, options-analysis, and brokerage-connected platform for active U.S. stock, ETF, and options traders. It is strongest for users who want streaming charts, EasyScan, formula-based PCF screening, real-time watchlists, customizable alerts, MT Newswires, paper trading, and options P&L workflows in one interface. Plans are paid, and several real-time or higher-capacity feeds are separate add-ons. TC2000 is U.S.-centric and built for active trading workflows, not broad global fundamental research or long-term portfolio accounting.

tools.name: BamSEC
tools.summary: BamSEC is a web-based SEC filings and transcripts research platform for investors and analysts who need faster EDGAR workflows. It is strongest for document search, filing redlines, table extraction, transcripts, insider and institutional ownership, watchlists, alerts, highlights, and source-link sharing, with most professional workflows gated behind Pro or Enterprise.

tools.name: StockFetcher
tools.summary: StockFetcher is a low-cost, text-based U.S. stock screener for traders who prefer writing plain-English technical filters instead of clicking through a modern visual screener. It is strongest for repeatable end-of-day or delayed-intraday scans built from 125+ technical indicators, saved filters, watchlists, CSV imports and exports, charts, and daily emailed results. Standard and Advanced differ by saved-filter limits, watchlist capacity, CSV export size, symbol-list size, and advanced filter syntax. It is powerful for its niche, but the interface is dated and it is not a real-time scanner or global multi-asset platform.

tools.name: Tiingo
tools.summary: Tiingo is an API-first market data provider for developers, quants, and small teams that need transparent flat-rate access to prices, fundamentals, corporate actions, news, forex, and crypto data. It is strongest when the user wants JSON, CSV, REST, WebSocket, Python, and AmiBroker-friendly data access rather than a consumer portfolio app. Free and paid plans differ by endpoint access, usage limits, history, and commercial rights. Tiingo is not a broker, portfolio tracker, research terminal, or blanket redistribution license; users need the right plan for business and commercial use.

tools.name: Yahoo Finance
tools.summary: Yahoo Finance is the familiar free market portal for quotes, business news, watchlists, portfolios, charts, screeners, and basic company research. It works best for mainstream investors who want a quick read on markets, holdings, earnings, analyst expectations, and news without learning a specialist terminal. My Portfolio adds manual portfolios, watchlists, CSV import/export, and supported brokerage linking. Premium plans add portfolio analytics, premium research, stock ideas, screeners, historical downloads, and reduced ads, but data delays and subscription availability vary by market.

tools.name: Charles Schwab
tools.summary: Charles Schwab is a major U.S. brokerage with commission-free online stock and ETF trading, broad account types, research tools, screeners, tax workflows, and the thinkorswim platform suite for active traders. It is strongest for investors who want one regulated brokerage relationship for long-term investing, options, futures, forex, paper trading, alerts, market data, and developer-authorized Trader API workflows. Many core tools are free with an approved account. Schwab is a broker, not an open market-data API or generic portfolio app.

tools.name: Sure Dividend
tools.summary: Sure Dividend is a dividend-focused research publisher for long-term income investors who want curated newsletters, dividend-growth stock ideas, valuation work, ranking spreadsheets, and downloadable dividend lists. It is strongest for users who prefer analyst-written reports and income-security screens over a do-it-yourself data terminal. The Sure Analysis Research Database is the top tier, combining premium services, 900+ reports, daily ranking spreadsheets, historical reports, and weekly updates. It is not a brokerage, live portfolio tracker, tax-lot system, or broad trading platform.

tools.name: Dividend.com
tools.summary: Dividend.com is a dividend research, screening, ratings, and watchlist site for income investors. It can be used to find dividend-paying stocks, ETFs, funds, REITs, MLPs, and preferreds, compare income ideas, and follow ex-dividend dates without using a full brokerage or portfolio accounting platform.

tools.name: Digrin
tools.summary: Digrin is a freemium web-based dividend portfolio tracker for dividend growth investors who want income calendars, portfolio statistics, tax estimates, DRIP handling, stock financials, and broker or CSV imports. It is strongest for self-directed dividend tracking, especially for Trading212 and Interactive Brokers users, but it is not a brokerage platform or broad research terminal.

tools.name: Dividend Watch
tools.summary: Dividend Watch is a web-based dividend and portfolio tracker for long-term income investors who want dividend forecasts, calendars, DRIP tracking, safety scores, stock and ETF research, and broker sync in one place. It is strongest for dividend portfolio planning and paid safety-score workflows, while the free tier is intentionally small and the platform is not a broker or real-time market terminal.

tools.name: Dividend Wealth
tools.summary: Dividend Wealth is a web-based dividend portfolio tracker and research platform for investors who want income forecasts, dividend scorecards, a screener, calendar tools, and optional Plaid brokerage linking. It is useful when dividend cash-flow planning matters more than active trading or broad terminal coverage.

tools.name: DivTracker
tools.summary: DivTracker is a dividend portfolio tracker for web and iOS users who want income views, upcoming payouts, ex-dividend dates, alerts, CSV export, and optional U.S. brokerage linking. It supports dividend cash-flow tracking rather than broad research, trading, or tax accounting.

tools.name: OnlyDividends
tools.summary: OnlyDividends is a privacy-first dividend-income tracker for investors who want to manually enter holdings, monitor dividend paydays, estimate net income after withholding tax, and visualize income trends without connecting a broker or bank. It is strongest for dividend investors who value simple portfolio income tracking, mobile access, multi-currency support, dividend calendars, health scores, and public dividend-stock pages. Free access tracks a small portfolio, while Premium raises the stock limit and adds priority support. It is not a brokerage, tax-lot system, rebalancer, public API, or full portfolio accounting product.

tools.name: Simply Wall St
tools.summary: Simply Wall St is a visual stock analysis and portfolio platform for long-term investors who prefer guided fundamental summaries over raw data tables. It is best known for its Snowflake-style company reports, global stock ideas, fair value views, dividend analysis, portfolio diagnostics, broker imports, and easy-to-scan visual research.

tools.name: Robinhood
tools.summary: Robinhood is an app-first U.S. brokerage for self-directed trading in stocks, ETFs, options, futures, and crypto, with an optional Robinhood Gold subscription for added research, cash, margin, derivatives, IRA, mortgage, card, and managed-strategy perks. It is strongest for users who prioritize simple mobile access and low-friction account workflows over advanced research, tax, or institutional trading tools. Standard securities trading is commission-free, but Gold, options, futures, crypto routing, staking, margin, managed strategies, and regulatory fees can change the economics. Robinhood is a broker, not an independent research terminal or tax platform.

tools.name: Interactive Brokers (IBKR)
tools.summary: Interactive Brokers (IBKR) is a global multi-asset brokerage platform for active investors, professionals, quants, and institutions who need broad market access, advanced order types, SmartRouting, APIs, paper trading, and portfolio analytics. It is strongest for serious execution and automation workflows, but commissions, market-data subscriptions, product availability, and API limits vary by market, account type, and jurisdiction.

tools.name: Fidelity (Fidelity Brokerage Services LLC)
tools.summary: Fidelity is a large U.S. brokerage for investors who want execution, account infrastructure, research, mobile apps, active-trader tools, options, bonds, mutual funds, fractional shares, and crypto inside one financial institution. It is strongest when brokerage access matters as much as research: $0 online U.S. stock and ETF trades sit alongside Fidelity Trader+, Active Trader Pro, streaming data, Level II, conditional orders, international trading, and integrated account reporting. It is not a public trading API or pure research terminal, and some workflows still carry contract, bond, crypto, regulatory, professional, or select ETF service fees.

tools.name: Webull
tools.summary: Webull is a U.S. app-first brokerage with mobile, desktop, and browser trading, strong charts and screeners, options tools, and selected fractional U.S. stocks and ETFs. Standard online U.S.-listed stock and ETF commissions are $0, but product, regulatory, exchange, and transfer charges still matter. Its optional Cash Management bank sweep is useful for eligible settled cash, though the current variable APY is visible only in the app.

tools.name: E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley
tools.summary: E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley is a broad U.S. brokerage for taxable, retirement, custodial, trust, estate, and business accounts. It combines $0 online U.S.-listed stock and ETF commissions with Power E*TRADE, options, mutual funds, bonds, research, selected fractional securities, and extensive tax and transfer infrastructure. Its standard bank sweep is convenient but currently pays a low APY for most balances.

tools.name: Merrill Edge
tools.summary: Merrill Edge is a U.S. self-directed brokerage closely integrated with Bank of America. It offers $0 online stock and ETF commissions, options, funds, bonds, retirement accounts, research, and MarketPro tools, with fast eligible transfers between linked banking and investing accounts. Its standard cash sweep is convenient but low-yielding, and the reviewed official materials do not establish retail fractional-share orders.

tools.name: Vanguard Brokerage
tools.summary: Vanguard Brokerage is built for U.S. long-term and retirement investors who want Vanguard funds alongside stocks, ETFs, options, bonds, and third-party funds. Online stock and ETF commissions are $0, and Vanguard ETF fractions start at $1. The platform is less trading-centric than active-broker rivals, and users must distinguish the FDIC Cash Deposit sweep from the VMFXX money-market settlement security and separate Cash Plus product.

tools.name: CommSec
tools.summary: CommSec is Commonwealth Bank's Australian self-directed brokerage, with CHESS-sponsored domestic shares and a separate custodied international account. Domestic pricing depends on settlement method, while international trading adds market-based brokerage and 0.55% FX.

tools.name: Stake
tools.summary: Stake gives eligible Australian residents direct CHESS-sponsored ASX trading and a separate DriveWealth U.S. account. Brokerage is A$3 or US$3 up to 30,000, U.S. fractions start at US$10, and ordinary cash earns no customer interest.

tools.name: Pearler
tools.summary: Pearler is an Australian long-term investing platform with CHESS-sponsored ASX holdings, custodied U.S. shares and automation. Direct buys and sells cost A$6.50, U.S. fractions are supported, and optional enrolled USD cash earns a variable rate.

tools.name: Selfwealth
tools.summary: Selfwealth offers CHESS-sponsored ASX trading plus custodied U.S. and Hong Kong access for Australian tax residents. It uses flat transaction fees, supports several entity accounts, pays no interest on cash, and does not offer fractional shares.

tools.name: Wealthsimple
tools.summary: Wealthsimple Trade is a Canadian self-directed brokerage with $0 online commissions for Canadian and U.S. listed stocks and ETFs, $1 fractional orders, registered and non-registered accounts, and optional USD accounts. Currency conversion and specialized transaction fees remain important, while chequing, savings, managed investing, and crypto are separate products.

tools.name: Qtrade Direct Investing
tools.summary: Qtrade Direct Investing is a Canadian self-directed broker for stocks, ETFs, options, mutual funds and fixed income. Current online equity, ETF and mutual-fund commissions are $0, with paid options contracts and specialized account, product, FX and service charges. Its research and portfolio-analysis tools complement a broad Canadian account range.

tools.name: National Bank Direct Brokerage
tools.summary: National Bank Direct Brokerage offers Canadian residents $0 online commissions on Canadian and U.S. stocks and ETFs, plus options, mutual funds and fixed income. Its CAD/USD accounts span non-registered and major Canadian registered registrations. Annual administration, options, FX, transfer and service charges remain important to total cost.

tools.name: TD Direct Investing
tools.summary: TD Direct Investing is a Canadian self-directed brokerage for stocks, ETFs, options, mutual funds and fixed income. Standard whole-share stock trades cost $9.99, eligible partial shares cost $1.99, and selected ETFs trade commission-free. WebBroker, mobile access, research, registered accounts and TD-integrated funding make it a broad platform rather than a free-trading app.

tools.name: CIBC Investor's Edge
tools.summary: CIBC Investor's Edge combines a Canadian bank brokerage with web and mobile trading, research, registered accounts and linked-bank funding. Standard stock and ETF trades cost $6.95, active traders can qualify for $4.95, and more than 180 named ETFs can meet commission-free conditions. Options, FX and account fees remain part of total cost.

tools.name: Groww
tools.summary: Groww is an India-resident self-directed broker for NSE/BSE shares and ETFs, mutual funds, IPOs, equity derivatives and MCX commodity contracts. Accounts have no opening or maintenance fee, while equity orders, derivatives, DP debits and optional MTF each have separate charges.

tools.name: Rakuten Securities
tools.summary: Rakuten Securities serves Japan residents with Japanese and overseas stocks, ETFs, funds, bonds and derivatives. Its Zero Course can remove domestic-stock commissions under SOR/R-Cross conditions, while U.S. securities cost 0.495% up to $22 and Kabumini provides eligible Japanese odd lots from one share.

tools.name: SBI Securities
tools.summary: SBI Securities is a broad Japan-resident brokerage for Japanese and overseas securities, funds, bonds and derivatives. Zero Revolution can make domestic cash, margin and S-share brokerage ¥0 under electronic-delivery conditions, while U.S. stock and ETF trades cost 0.495% up to $22.

tools.name: Monex Securities
tools.summary: Monex Securities serves Japan residents with Japanese and U.S. stocks, ETFs, funds, bonds and derivatives. Domestic per-order commissions run from ¥55 to ¥1,070, U.S. stock and ETF trades cost 0.495% up to $22, and eligible Japanese odd lots trade from one share through One Share.

tools.name: Nubank Investments
tools.summary: Nubank Investments brings Nu Investimentos brokerage into the Nubank app for eligible Brazil residents. Digital stock, BDR and other listed-security brokerage and Nu custody are R$0, with B3 and product charges separate; Brazilian tax reporting is unified with the wider Nubank relationship.

tools.name: RBC Direct Investing
tools.summary: RBC Direct Investing combines a Canadian bank brokerage with web and mobile trading, research, registered accounts and fast RBC funding. Full-Suite stock and ETF trades cost $9.95, active traders can qualify for $6.95, and selected ETFs can meet $0-commission conditions. Options, FX and product costs still affect total cost.

tools.name: BMO InvestorLine
tools.summary: BMO InvestorLine combines web and mobile self-directed trading with research, broad Canadian account support and linked BMO funding. Standard stock and ETF trades cost $9.95, active traders can qualify for $3.95, and more than 100 selected ETFs can meet $0-commission conditions. FX and low-balance account fees remain relevant.

tools.name: SoFi Invest
tools.summary: SoFi Self-Directed Invest combines a beginner-friendly brokerage with stocks, ETFs, options, mutual funds, selected alternative funds, and more than 4,000 fractional securities. Standard online commissions are $0, though fund, transfer, inactivity, regulatory, and other service charges remain important. The optional brokerage bank sweep is separate from SoFi Checking and Savings.

tools.name: SMARTBROKER+
tools.summary: SMARTBROKER+ combines a German self-directed securities account with broad exchange access and low-cost gettex execution. Custody is free, eligible gettex orders from €500 can cost €0, and eligible savings-plan executions are free. The exact venue, order size, currency and product determine actual cost, while the advertised interest account remains separate from brokerage settlement cash.

tools.name: MyInvestor
tools.summary: MyInvestor combines Spanish banking with a self-directed stock and ETF broker. Standard stock and ETF trades cost 0.12% with €3 and €1 minimums respectively, while custody and inactivity are free. It handles Spanish tax reporting and U.S. dividend paperwork, but does not offer fractional shares and limits access outside Spain to eligible Spanish nationals resident in the EU.

tools.name: BUX
tools.summary: BUX is an app-first European stock and ETF broker available in eight countries. It supports whole and fractional investing plus commission-free monthly Investment Plan purchases. Its three tiers trade off monthly and asset-based fees, order types, FX markups and cash interest, making plan choice central to the real cost.

tools.name: Public.com
tools.summary: Public combines self-directed stocks, ETFs, bonds, and options with recurring Investment Plans and optional Premium access. Regular-hours U.S.-listed equity trades carry $0 commission, while extended-hours, OTC, plan, transfer, and regulatory fees still matter. Its High-Yield Cash Account is a separate secondary brokerage account, not ordinary free cash or a savings account.

tools.name: Firstrade
tools.summary: Firstrade offers U.S. and supported international investors online stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, options, and fixed income through a web and mobile brokerage. Its stated online commissions for stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, and options are $0, although regulatory, fund, short-borrow, fixed-income, transfer, and service costs remain. International eligibility is limited to an explicit 27-country matrix.

tools.name: Freetrade
tools.summary: Freetrade is an app-first UK broker offering commission-free dealing across a GIA, Stocks and Shares ISA, Junior Stocks and Shares ISA, and SIPP. Basic is free; Standard and Plus trade a monthly subscription for lower FX fees, higher capped cash interest, and service extras. It suits long-term self-directed investors more than users needing margin, derivatives, or global multi-currency cash accounts.

tools.name: Hargreaves Lansdown
tools.summary: Hargreaves Lansdown is a broad UK investment platform for investors who want funds, listed securities, research, service, and a deep range of tax wrappers in one place. It is strongest for account breadth and administration, not lowest-cost frequent trading: platform, dealing, and FX charges all matter.

tools.name: interactive investor
tools.summary: interactive investor is a flat-fee UK platform for self-directed Trading Accounts, ISAs, SIPPs, Junior ISAs, and family portfolios. Its Core, Plus, and Premium subscriptions suit investors who value predictable platform charges and broad global choice, but trade, FX, and special-service costs still vary by plan.

tools.name: DEGIRO
tools.summary: DEGIRO is an execution-only European online broker for self-directed investors who want low-cost access to stocks, ETFs, bonds, funds, options, futures, and other listed products across many markets. It is strongest for cost-conscious European brokerage access and basic portfolio administration, not for investment advice, managed portfolios, deep research, or official API-based automation.

tools.name: Value Investors Club (VIC)
tools.summary: Value Investors Club is a selective, free investment-idea community built around long-form value-investing writeups and member discussion rather than paid newsletters or screeners. It is strongest for investors who want deep fundamental pitches, peer feedback, long/short idea archives, and a high-signal community model. VIC is not verified investment advice, a data terminal, a broker, or a paid research product.

tools.name: Beanvest
tools.summary: Beanvest is a quality-investing research app for long-term investors who want opinionated stock reports, a proprietary Quality Score, component scores, fair value labels, and a compact quality-stock screener. It is strongest for investors who like a framework around moat, pricing power, predictability, financial strength, capital allocation, and management, but coverage is selective, premium fair-value data is gated, and there is no free trial or refund policy.

tools.name: DATAROMA
tools.summary: DATAROMA is a free, focused tracker for superinvestor 13F portfolios, recent portfolio changes, and insider buying activity. It supports value-investing idea discovery and manager-following workflows, then verify timing, filings, and fundamentals before acting.

tools.name: Stockopedia
tools.summary: Stockopedia is a paid stock research and screening platform for investors who want StockRanks, StockReports, GuruScreens, factor-style idea generation, portfolio Folios, alerts, and exportable screen data across selected regions. It is strongest for disciplined Quality, Value, and Momentum screening rather than broker execution or API-based data delivery.

tools.name: Screener.in
tools.summary: Screener.in is an India-focused stock screener and fundamental-research platform for investors who want company pages, custom financial queries, watchlists, alerts, exports, filings, shareholding data, and Screener AI. It is strongest for Indian equity research where users care about query-language screens, decade-long fundamentals, quarterly-result alerts, corporate announcements, and mobile access. The free Hobby Investor plan is useful, while Active Investor Premium adds exports, more alerts, peer comparison depth, segment data, concall notes, product trends, and AI credits. It is not a global broker, trade-execution platform, or unlimited AI workspace.

tools.name: The Motley Fool
tools.summary: The Motley Fool is a long-running investing publisher and stock-picking membership business for retail investors who want plain-English market commentary, education, watchlists, portfolios, and curated stock recommendations. It is strongest for users who prefer monthly recommendation services and model-portfolio style guidance over raw data, APIs, or custom valuation tooling. Free articles, podcasts, and market pages sit alongside paid tiers such as Stock Advisor, Epic, Epic Plus, Fool Portfolios, and Fool One. It is not a broker, institutional research terminal, tax tool, or personalized portfolio manager.

tools.name: Morningstar Investor
tools.summary: Morningstar Investor is a subscription research product for long-term investors who want Morningstar ratings, analyst reports, fair value estimates, moat research, screeners, and portfolio analysis. It is especially useful for comparing stocks, funds, and ETFs through Morningstar’s proprietary research framework rather than for active trading or broker-connected portfolio automation.

tools.name: Magic Formula Investing
tools.summary: Magic Formula Investing is the official free Joel Greenblatt-style stock screener based on the Magic Formula strategy from The Little Book That Beats the Market. It ranks U.S.-listed non-financial, non-utility stocks using earnings yield and return on capital, then returns a simple list of 30 or 50 names based on the user’s minimum market-cap input. It is intentionally narrow: use it for value-quality idea generation, not as a flexible stock research terminal, portfolio tool, broker, or investment advice.

tools.name: FINVIZ
tools.summary: FINVIZ is best known as a fast U.S. stock screener with heat maps, quote pages, insider activity, news, and portfolio watchlists. It works well when you want to move from a broad market view to a tighter list of stocks using both fundamental and technical filters. The free version is useful for delayed research; FINVIZ Elite is the serious workflow upgrade for real-time quotes, intraday charts, alerts, exports, advertised API access, and deeper ETF and portfolio tools.

tools.name: Finbox
tools.summary: Finbox is a web-based stock and ETF research platform for investors who want global screening, financial statements, fair-value estimates, valuation models, watchlists, investor portfolios, and spreadsheet exports in one workflow. It is strongest for valuation-led research: screens can lead into normalized financials, DCF and comparable-company models, dividend and earnings trackers, peer charts, and exportable model templates. It is not a public API product, and costs can rise with regions and Data Boost when exports or broader market coverage matter.

tools.name: FAST Graphs
tools.summary: FAST Graphs is a fundamentals-first stock research platform built around visual valuation charts, earnings, cash flow, dividends, forecasts, and portfolio views. It is useful when long-term valuation and business fundamentals matter more than intraday trading tools.

tools.name: Portfolio123
tools.summary: Portfolio123 is a rules-based quant research and portfolio-management platform for investors who want stock and ETF screeners, ranking systems, factor research, realistic backtests, strategy simulations, portfolio tracking, broker connectivity, and API/DataMiner access. It is strongest for systematic investors who want point-in-time research workflows without building everything from code.

tools.name: GuruFocus
tools.summary: GuruFocus is a value-investing research platform for investors who want global fundamentals, valuation tools, GF Score, GF Value, stock/ETF/bond screeners, backtesting, guru and institutional holdings, insider trades, portfolio tracking, spreadsheet add-ins, and data/API access. It is strongest for fundamental and value-oriented research rather than brokerage execution.

tools.name: Khan Academy (Economics & Finance)
tools.summary: Khan Academy Economics & Finance is a free education hub for learning economics, finance, capital markets, financial literacy, personal finance, and basic investing concepts before using more advanced investment tools. It is best for beginners, students, educators, and product onboarding paths where users need clear lessons, videos, articles, and practice exercises without a paywall. It does not provide market data, screeners, portfolios, analyst research, trading, or professional investment credentials.

tools.name: MarketWatch
tools.summary: MarketWatch is a Dow Jones financial-news and consumer market-data portal for stock market news, quote pages, watchlists, screeners, calendars, BigCharts, options chains, fund research, rates, newsletters, and paper trading through Virtual Stock Exchange. It is useful for retail investors who want mainstream market coverage and lightweight tools in one familiar site. Treat the subscription mainly as journalism access: market-data pages remain consumer-grade, exchange delays apply, and MarketWatch is not a broker, professional terminal, public API, or modeling platform.

tools.name: MarketScreener
tools.summary: MarketScreener is a broad global market news and stock research portal with quotes, watchlists, screeners, charts, calendars, analyst data, company financials, transcripts, ESG ratings, insider data, newsletters, and model portfolio content. It is useful for retail investors who want one content-heavy site for daily monitoring and global stock discovery. The tradeoff is tier gating: advanced screeners, reports, portfolios, decision-support tools, and some content require paid Access, Premium, or Expert subscriptions, with pricing that can vary by region and promotion.

tools.name: Unusual Whales
tools.summary: Unusual Whales is an options-flow and market-activity platform for traders who want real-time U.S. options trades, dark pool/off-exchange activity, alerts, screeners, news, congressional trading data, and developer API access. It is strongest for alert-driven options and order-flow research, with portfolio tracking, API, WebSocket streaming, and historical full-market options data handled through separate paid surfaces.

tools.name: OptionStrat
tools.summary: OptionStrat is an options strategy builder, profit calculator, optimizer, and unusual-flow scanner for traders who want to model payoff diagrams, Greeks, event dates, saved strategies, alerts, and flow in one web and mobile workflow. It is strongest for options-specific research: comparing strategies, estimating probability of profit, scanning unusual contracts, and tracking trades visually. Free access uses delayed quotes and limited flow, while Live Tools and Live Flow unlock real-time builder features, broader flow, alerts, news, insider and Congress trades, and futures options flow. It is not a brokerage, broad portfolio system, or live-data product for professional users.

tools.name: Portfolio Visualizer
tools.summary: Portfolio Visualizer is a web-based portfolio analysis suite for backtesting portfolios, testing asset allocations, running Monte Carlo simulations, optimizing allocations, analyzing factors, checking correlations, and researching funds. It is strongest for DIY investors, analysts, and advisors who want evidence for allocation, withdrawal, and risk decisions without building every model in spreadsheets. The free tier is useful but constrained, while Basic and Pro add larger portfolios, YTD results, saving, imports, exports, and commercial-use support on Pro. It is not a broker, live portfolio accounting system, or automatic rebalancing platform.

tools.name: Portfolio Performance
tools.summary: Portfolio Performance is a free, open-source, local-first desktop portfolio tracker for investors who want detailed performance accounting, TTWROR/IRR reporting, multi-currency support, rebalancing, imports, exports, and privacy without broker credential sync. It is strongest for hands-on investors willing to maintain transactions locally, while the mobile app is mainly a read-only companion unless optional dashboard subscriptions are used.

tools.name: Testfol.io
tools.summary: Testfol.io is a freemium web-based portfolio backtesting and analysis toolkit for investors who want to test allocations, cashflows, rebalancing rules, tactical signals, leverage, correlations, and historical risk/return. It is strongest for portfolio-level experimentation rather than intraday monitoring or live account management. Anonymous and free-account use remain available, while Pro and Pro+ unlock advanced analytics, higher limits, uploads, downloads, alerts, and cloud workflows. Backtests depend on historical assumptions and end-of-day data, so they are not trade execution or forward-looking guarantees.

tools.name: Investing.com
tools.summary: Investing.com is a global market portal for investors who want quotes, charts, financial news, an economic calendar, watchlists, alerts, portfolio tracking, screeners, and mobile market monitoring in one place. The free site is strongest as a broad market dashboard, while InvestingPro adds the paid research layer with AI tools, stock ideas, fair value estimates, Health Scores, ProTips, and deeper fundamentals.

tools.name: Investopedia
tools.summary: Investopedia is a free finance education and market news publisher with a widely searched Stock Simulator for paper trading. It is best for beginners, students, educators, and self-directed investors who want definitions, explainers, market context, newsletters, calculators, and a virtual-money environment before using a real brokerage account. The simulator is useful for practice, but it uses delayed data, limited exchange coverage, and limited options functionality, so it should not be treated as live execution, professional trading infrastructure, or investment advice.

tools.name: MacroMicro
tools.summary: MacroMicro is a global macro and market analytics workspace for investors who want economic cycle charts, macro dashboards, ETF tools, institutional holdings views, COT flow, event calendars, correlation charts, lightweight backtesting, and AI-powered earnings summaries. It is strongest as a visual macro research platform with paid export and API paths. Constraints include licensing: downloads, API access, watermark-free commercial chart use, and commercial reuse rights are gated to higher-priced plans.

tools.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data)
tools.summary: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) is the free macroeconomic time-series database from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, used by students, investors, analysts, quants, and product builders who need trusted economic data, charts, release calendars, Excel access, mobile apps, and a REST API. It is strongest for official macro context around inflation, rates, GDP, employment, exchange rates, credit, and market indicators rather than equity fundamentals or brokerage workflows. API users need a free API key, and usage remains subject to FRED terms and source-specific data restrictions.

tools.name: Trading Economics
tools.summary: Trading Economics is a macro and markets data platform for browsing economic indicators, calendars, forecasts, market data, company financials, news, ratings, and corporate events, with paid REST API, WebSocket, spreadsheet, BI, and AI-assistant integrations. It is strongest for developers, analysts, and teams building dashboards, alerts, research apps, and macro data pipelines from one source. Guest credentials provide limited sample access, while Standard, Professional, and Enterprise plans govern real API use, streaming, rate limits, row limits, and commercial rights. It is data infrastructure, not a broker or investment-advice service.

tools.name: Trading 212
tools.summary: Trading 212 is an app-first multi-entity broker for direct stock and ETF investing, fractional orders, recurring Pies, and—in the UK—Stocks and Shares ISA and SIPP wrappers. It also offers a separate CFD product. Invest, ISA, and SIPP trades have zero Trading 212 commission and custody fees; FX, taxes, spreads, financing, and external market costs can still apply.

tools.name: Alpha Vantage
tools.summary: Alpha Vantage is an API-first financial data provider for developers, students, quants, and analysts who need a simple API key for stock, ETF, mutual fund, FX, crypto, options, commodities, fundamentals, news, sentiment, and macroeconomic datasets. It is strongest for learning, prototypes, spreadsheets, and personal API workflows, but the free quota is small, premium endpoints require membership, and commercial use needs separate licensing.

tools.name: YCharts
tools.summary: YCharts is an advisor- and asset-manager-focused investment research, portfolio analytics, proposal, reporting, and client-communication platform. It is strongest for professionals who need client-ready charts, comparison tables, model portfolios, portfolio optimization, scenarios, stress tests, Monte Carlo analysis, Excel workflows, proposal generation, and firm sharing controls. Public pricing is sales-led on the current plans page, with several datasets and modules represented as add-ons. YCharts is not built as a casual free screener, brokerage account, or low-cost consumer portfolio tracker.

tools.name: Quiver Quantitative
tools.summary: Quiver Quantitative is an alternative-data platform for investors who want dashboards, screeners, alerts, backtests, and API access around political trading, insider activity, institutional holdings, lobbying, government contracts, patents, app data, ETF exposure, dark-pool activity, and related datasets. It is strongest when conventional fundamentals are not enough and users want differentiated public-disclosure signals. Web Premium and Quiver API are separate products with different prices, trials, dataset tiers, and commercial-use rules. Alternative data can be noisy and lagged, so it needs validation before being treated as a signal.

tools.name: Seeking Alpha
tools.summary: Seeking Alpha is a stock research and investment news platform for investors who want market news, contributor analysis, Quant Ratings, analyst ratings, portfolio alerts, screeners, and earnings transcript research in one place. It is strongest for idea generation and ongoing monitoring, with Premium or PRO needed for deeper research, AI summaries, full transcripts, factor grades, and advanced portfolio tools.

tools.name: The Fly Pro
tools.summary: The Fly Pro is a visual stock research, company KPI, and real-time news platform that now receives traffic from the legacy Main Street Data URL. It is useful for investors who want company-specific operating metrics, financial charts, comparisons, earnings calendars, transcripts, analyst items, and news in one browser workspace. Deeper KPI history, transcripts, advanced charting, portfolios, and institutional workflows are tier-gated.

tools.name: TipRanks
tools.summary: TipRanks is an investment research platform built around analyst ratings, price targets, expert rankings, Smart Score, AI stock analysis, news sentiment, insider signals, hedge-fund activity, and portfolio tools. It is strongest for investors who want to compare market opinions and stock forecasts quickly, with Premium and Ultimate unlocking more of the expert, portfolio, export, and AI workflow.

tools.name: Total Real Returns
tools.summary: Total Real Returns is a free web tool for charting real purchasing-power returns and nominal total returns with dividends reinvested. It is strongest for investors who want a fast visual answer to how stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, or cash-like series performed after inflation instead of only seeing price charts. The site provides return tables, drawdowns, normalization controls, and multi-symbol comparisons with end-of-day updates. It is intentionally narrow: not a screener, portfolio tracker, API, broker, or full research terminal.

tools.name: Stock Analysis
tools.summary: Stock Analysis is a web and mobile research hub for investors who want stock screeners, financial statements, earnings calendars, market news, charts, analyst forecasts, watchlists, and portfolio tracking in one approachable workspace. It is strongest as an everyday due-diligence layer for researching public companies, ETFs, mutual funds, IPOs, dividends, corporate actions, and market movers without needing a professional terminal. Free access is useful but ad-supported and limited; Pro and Unlimited add broader history, saved screeners, alerts, exports, full ETF holdings, broker sync, advanced analyst filtering, and higher watchlist or download limits. It is not a broker, advisory service, portfolio accounting system, public API, custom quant platform, or data redistribution source.

tools.name: Stock Rover
tools.summary: Stock Rover is a web-based stock, ETF, fund, and portfolio research platform for investors who want 800+ financial metrics, 20 years of historical fundamentals, deep portfolio analytics, dividend tracking, automated DCF-driven intrinsic value and Margin of Safety tools, printable research reports, stock ratings, broker-linked portfolios, and alerts. It is strongest for North American fundamental research and portfolio management, not for trade execution or full strategy backtesting.

tools.name: TradingView
tools.summary: TradingView is a chart-first market analysis platform for traders who want powerful charts, screeners, alerts, Pine Script, paper trading, and broker-connected trading across many asset classes. It is strongest when technical analysis, custom indicators, strategy testing, watchlists, and real-time market monitoring are part of the same workflow. The free Basic plan is useful for trying the product, but active users usually run into limits on charts, indicators, alerts, watchlists, and historical bars. Some real-time exchange data is sold separately.

tools.name: TrendSpider
tools.summary: TrendSpider is a paid, browser-based analysis and automation platform for active traders who want automated technical analysis, multi-timeframe scanning, strategy testing, alerts, bots, AI tools, and alternative data in one workspace. It is strongest for intermediate and advanced U.S. stock, ETF, options, futures, forex, and crypto workflows. It is not a broker, and live order routing depends on SignalStack plus a supported broker or exchange. Plan limits, paid trials, optional data fees, Sidekick message costs, and backtest assumptions deserve close review before subscribing.

tools.name: OptionCharts
tools.summary: OptionCharts is a web-based options analytics workspace for visualizing strategy payoff, Greeks, implied-volatility skew, expected moves, gamma and delta exposure, contract history, and market-wide options trends. It is best for traders who want options research and chart exports, not brokerage execution, a public options-data API, or guaranteed real-time access on every plan.

tools.name: Damodaran - Cost of Capital by Sector (US)
tools.summary: Damodaran - Cost of Capital by Sector is a free NYU Stern industry WACC table for analysts who need a credible sector baseline for DCF models and cost-of-capital work. It provides beta, cost of equity, cost of debt, capital structure, tax-rate, and WACC estimates by U.S. industry, but it is an annual spreadsheet-style dataset rather than a company-specific WACC engine or live market-data tool.

tools.name: FDIC BankFind Suite (BankFind)
tools.summary: FDIC BankFind Suite is the official free FDIC source for looking up FDIC-insured banks, branches, histories, structure changes, failures, financials, Summary of Deposits data, APIs, and bulk downloads. It is useful when bank research needs primary-source U.S. government data rather than a commercial bank screener.

tools.name: ECB Data Portal
tools.summary: ECB Data Portal is the official free European Central Bank source for ECB statistics, euro area macro data, interest rates, exchange rates, yield curves, downloads, charts, and SDMX API access. It is useful when you need primary-source European macro data rather than a commercial terminal summary.

tools.name: CME FedWatch
tools.summary: CME FedWatch is the widely used CME Group tool for tracking market-implied probabilities of Federal Reserve target-rate outcomes for upcoming FOMC meetings, derived from 30-Day Fed Funds futures. It is strongest for macro investors, rates teams, journalists, and dashboards monitoring Fed-rate expectations, with a free web tool plus paid EOD and intraday API options, but probabilities are market-implied estimates, not Fed guidance or investment advice.

tools.name: BIS Data Portal
tools.summary: BIS Data Portal is the official free statistics portal from the Bank for International Settlements for global macro-financial time series, exports, bulk downloads, release calendars, charts, tables, and SDMX API access. It is strongest for analysts, students, quants, and builders who need cross-country banking, credit, debt, derivatives, liquidity, property-price, exchange-rate, and central-bank statistics, but it is an official macro data source rather than an equity terminal or trading platform.

tools.name: ETF Insider
tools.summary: ETF Insider is a web-based ETF, mutual fund, and stock portfolio visualization tool for investors who want to see holdings overlap, concentration, correlations, factor exposure, and efficient-frontier style portfolio tradeoffs. It is strongest for diagnosing hidden ETF overlap in U.S.-listed portfolios, with full holdings depth, Excel export, API access, and white-label options gated by Pro or Enterprise plans.

tools.name: ETF Central
tools.summary: ETF Central is a free ETF research and education site for screening, comparing, watching, and learning about U.S.-listed ETFs. It supports approachable ETF discovery, segment flows, portfolio building, news, and ETF education before moving to execution or deeper portfolio accounting elsewhere.

tools.name: Trackinsight
tools.summary: Trackinsight is a global ETF research and data platform for screening, comparing, monitoring, and analyzing ETFs and ETF portfolios. It is strongest when the job is ETF due diligence, ESG/factor context, portfolio insight, or licensed ETF data delivery, not single-stock research, options analytics, broker execution, or an unrestricted public API.

tools.name: MarketXLS
tools.summary: MarketXLS is an Excel-first market data, options, portfolio analytics, screening, and template add-in for investors who want live or delayed financial data directly inside spreadsheets. It is useful for Excel-heavy workflows covering stocks, ETFs, options, mutual funds, crypto, forex, fundamentals, FRED economic data, ETF holdings, portfolio templates, and broker order-ticket integrations. It is not a redistributable market-data API: real-time coverage is tiered, some exchanges require add-ons, and licensing is personal-use oriented.

tools.name: Wisesheets
tools.summary: Wisesheets is a spreadsheet-first stock-analysis add-on for Excel and Google Sheets, built around formulas for company financials, key metrics, prices, dividends, analyst data, ETF/fund data, options chains, and broker-connected portfolio data. It is best for investors who want to build research models inside spreadsheets, with commercial use, faster data, and advanced screener workflows gated by plan.

tools.name: Winus
tools.summary: Winus is an AI-assisted financial research workspace for stock, market, macro, and cross-asset analysis. It is best evaluated as a source-traceable research assistant for finance professionals, not as a broker, standalone data terminal, public API, or replacement for verifying investment work.

tools.name: ETF Action
tools.summary: ETF Action is an ETF analytics platform for advisors, asset managers, and ETF-focused investors who need classification, look-through holdings, overlap, flows, model portfolios, 13F screening, exports, and enterprise data workflows. It is useful when ETF research and model construction need more depth than a free quote page.

tools.name: Sharesight
tools.summary: Sharesight is a global portfolio, dividend, performance, and tax-reporting tracker for DIY investors, accountants, advisers, and family offices. It is built for keeping investment records and reports across brokers and asset types, not for placing trades, running intraday trading dashboards, or replacing a tax professional in complex filings.

tools.name: Dune
tools.summary: Dune is a crypto and onchain analytics platform for SQL dashboards, decoded blockchain data, APIs, alerts, uploads, teams, and AI-agent workflows. It is useful when you want to build or automate custom onchain analysis across many blockchains rather than consume a fixed market-data screen.

tools.name: Glassnode
tools.summary: Glassnode is a digital-asset analytics platform for investors, analysts, quants, and institutions that need on-chain metrics, crypto market data, derivatives data, ETF data, alerts, research, workbench charts, exports, and API delivery. It is strongest when crypto-native data matters: wallet behavior, entity-adjusted metrics, point-in-time series, futures/options context, and institutional delivery options go beyond a general price chart. The main constraint is access gating: Studio Standard and Advanced are display-oriented, exports are Professional-only, and API or Excel workflows require Professional plus an API add-on and data credits.

tools.name: SEDAR+ (CSA Public Filings - Canada)
tools.summary: SEDAR+ is the official Canadian Securities Administrators public-filings system for Canadian issuer and investment-fund disclosure. It is useful when investors need primary-source Canadian filings, prospectuses, reporting-issuer status, cease-trade orders, or disciplined-list checks, but it is not a global filings terminal, broker, ticker-first screener, or public data API.

tools.name: USAspending
tools.summary: USAspending is the official U.S. federal spending open-data portal for awards, recipients, agencies, federal accounts, contracts, grants, loans, and other spending records. It helps investors and builders research government exposure and contractor trends, but it is not a securities dataset, ticker map, market-data feed, company fundamentals provider, or investment-advice tool.

tools.name: Visualping
tools.summary: Visualping is a website-change monitoring and alerting platform that investors, compliance teams, and analysts can use to watch regulator pages, investor-relations pages, pricing pages, competitor pages, and other web sources. It is best treated as a web-native monitoring layer, not a market-data feed, normalized financial database, broker, or guarantee that every page change is investment-relevant.

tools.name: OTC Markets
tools.summary: OTC Markets combines a public research website for U.S. OTC-traded securities with licensed market-data, disclosure, and feed products for professional users. It is useful for OTC issuer pages, tiers, quotes, news, filings, screeners, and Level 1/Level 2 data workflows, but it is not a full global equity terminal, broker, or free redistribution source.

tools.name: EveryTicker
tools.summary: EveryTicker is a free U.S. stock research platform focused on undercovered public companies, including microcaps, nanocaps, and OTC names. It supports fundamental reports, AI and traditional screening, watchlists, 13F ownership context, and investment-theme discovery before doing deeper diligence.

tools.name: InsiderScore (VerityData | InsiderScore)
tools.summary: InsiderScore, now part of VerityData, is an institutional research and data product for insider transactions, buybacks, management changes, institutional holdings, Form 144, 10b5-1 disclosures, and related event feeds. It is built for professional research teams that need cleansed and contextualized event data, not a self-serve retail app, broker, or raw free SEC filing viewer.

tools.name: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database
tools.summary: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database is the official free U.S. regulatory dataset for consumer financial complaints about banks, lenders, credit bureaus, fintechs, debt collectors, mortgage servicers, cards, payments, and other consumer-finance products. It is strongest for analysts who need complaint trends by company, product, issue, geography, response status, narrative availability, downloads, and API access, but complaints are submissions rather than verified findings.

tools.name: SEC EDGAR - Company Filings (Full‑Text Search & Search Filings)
tools.summary: SEC EDGAR Search is the official free source for U.S. public company, fund, insider, ownership, prospectus, and XBRL filing research. It is strongest as the source of truth for SEC filings, full-text search, latest filings, RSS feeds, CIK lookup, and data.sec.gov JSON APIs, but raw filings still require parsing and automated access must follow SEC fair-access rules.

tools.name: Open Payments (CMS)
tools.summary: Open Payments (CMS) is the official free U.S. database for Sunshine Act payment, research, and ownership disclosures between drug or device companies, GPOs, and covered healthcare providers. It supports healthcare investing, policy, compliance, and key-opinion-leader research when you need source-level evidence of manufacturer-provider relationships.

tools.name: Wayback Machine (Internet Archive)
tools.summary: Wayback Machine is the Internet Archive's web-archive service for saving, discovering, and citing historical versions of webpages. For investment research, it is useful for checking old IR pages, fund pages, pricing pages, product claims, and disclosure language, but it is not structured market data, guaranteed page coverage, or a substitute for verifying primary filings.

tools.name: Listen Notes
tools.summary: Listen Notes is a podcast search engine, podcast API, alerts product, and dataset provider that can be useful for investors, analysts, and builders treating podcasts as alternative research inputs. It can be used to search podcast metadata, monitor keyword mentions, build podcast discovery workflows, or buy/export podcast datasets for analysis. Podcast mentions are indirect evidence, so Listen Notes should complement financial statements, filings, market data, and verified sources rather than replace them.

tools.name: Stocknear
tools.summary: Stocknear is a lightweight U.S.-market stock, ETF, and options research platform with options flow, dark-pool context, analyst data, 13F holdings, congressional trades, earnings, news, alerts, and an AI Agent. It is best for retail-friendly research dashboards and active monitoring, not global multi-asset coverage, brokerage execution, tax-lot accounting, or a self-serve data API.

tools.name: Changeflow (Trackly)
tools.summary: Changeflow, formerly reached through Trackly, is an AI website-change intelligence platform for monitoring filings, regulator pages, IR pages, competitor pages, PDFs, feeds, and other online sources. It is useful for investment and compliance teams that want relevant briefings rather than raw page diffs, but it is not market data, trade execution, or a substitute for human review.

tools.name: IPO Watch (ipowatch.in)
tools.summary: IPO Watch is a free India IPO news and tracking site for mainboard IPOs, SME IPOs, IPO GMP, subscription updates, allotment guidance, listing outcomes, and related corporate-action news. It is a useful retail-friendly starting point for IPO calendars, GMP today queries, allotment-status workflows, and quick listing-gain context. Because GMP is unofficial and the site is not a broker or SEBI-registered advisory product, users should verify figures against official exchanges, registrars, RHPs, and broker application pages.

tools.name: IPOWala.in
tools.summary: India-focused IPO information portal (NSE/BSE context) with a live IPO Grey Market Premium (GMP) page and other IPO tracking pages (subscription status, allotment links, listing-performance tables, and buyback lists). GMP content is stated as informational only; the site states it does not trade, deal, or support grey-market / “subject-to” transactions, and recommends consulting a SEBI-registered advisor. The live GMP page returned HTTP 200 on 2026-07-01 and showed separate mainboard and SME GMP sections with updated timestamps.

tools.name: Groww - IPOs (Apply & Calendar)
tools.summary: Groww IPO is the IPO calendar and application workflow inside Groww for Indian retail investors who want to browse upcoming, open, and closed Indian IPOs, apply through UPI mandate, track allotment and listing status, and follow IPO-related updates from the same broker ecosystem. It is strongest when the user needs an action path from IPO discovery to application, not just IPO news. The workflow is India-specific and account-dependent: applying requires Groww brokerage/KYC eligibility, supported UPI behavior, and exchange or registrar processes, while Groww Trading API access is separate and does not document IPO apply endpoints.

tools.name: FXMacroData
tools.summary: FXMacroData is a real-time macroeconomic and central-bank data API for FX traders, quants, developers, and analysts who need timestamped releases, rates, yields, calendars, COT data, FX spot data, dashboards, MCP tools, embeddable charts, and exports. It is strongest when macro release timing and point-in-time history matter for backtests, dashboards, or live FX workflows. Free access is evaluation-oriented, full history and non-USD data are paid, Individual and Startup trials require a credit card, and redistribution rights are plan-gated.

tools.name: FX Replay
tools.summary: FX Replay is a browser-based manual backtesting and bar-replay platform for traders practicing forex, futures, crypto, commodities, and related multi-asset setups. It is strongest for discretionary strategy practice: replay sessions, multi-chart layouts, multi-pair testing, journaling, checklists, Monte Carlo, risk-reward simulation, CSV imports, and economic-calendar context help traders review execution without connecting a live broker. It is not an automated strategy engine, and seconds-level data plus broader asset coverage are Pro-gated.

tools.name: PwC - IPO Watch EMEA (all editions)
tools.summary: PwC IPO Watch EMEA is a free quarterly publication that summarizes IPO volume, proceeds, sectors, countries, exchanges, top deals, and market commentary across EMEA principal stock markets. It is useful for regional IPO context and citations, but it is a PDF-first report rather than a live IPO calendar, interactive screener, or public API.

tools.name: InvestorGain
tools.summary: InvestorGain is a free India primary-markets portal for IPO GMP, live IPO subscription status, allotment links, anchor investor data, IPO performance history, rights issues, NCDs, sovereign gold bonds, and broker comparisons. It is useful for retail investors checking mainboard and SME IPO demand signals before verifying official exchange, registrar, RHP, and broker details. Treat Grey Market Premium as unofficial sentiment data, not a guarantee of listing gains or a complete investment case.

tools.name: Chittorgarh.com
tools.summary: Chittorgarh.com is a long-running Indian primary-market portal for retail investors following IPOs, FPOs, NCDs, bonds, broker reviews, subscription data, and grey-market premium snapshots. It is strongest for quick India IPO context across web and mobile apps, but GMP is unofficial and unregulated, the site is publisher-style rather than a normalized database, and there is no public API.

tools.name: Simply Safe Dividends
tools.summary: Simply Safe Dividends is a dividend-focused research and portfolio tracker built around 0-100 Dividend Safety Scores, income forecasts, dividend alerts, screeners, valuation charts, and portfolio monitoring. It is strongest for U.S.-focused income investors who want to avoid dividend cuts, but it is a paid research product after trial, not a broker, tax engine, or public data API.

tools.name: Calcbench
tools.summary: Calcbench is a professional SEC filing, XBRL, financial statement, disclosure, and Excel research platform for analysts who need traceable as-filed numbers, standardized accounting metrics, footnotes, redlines, proxy data, compensation data, M&A details, and API access. It is strongest for accounting-heavy U.S. equity research and data workflows, but meaningful access is priced for professional users and API access is sold separately from standard subscriptions.

tools.name: Visible Alpha
tools.summary: Visible Alpha, now part of S&P Global Market Intelligence, is an enterprise consensus and model-derived data platform built from full sell-side analyst models. It is useful for line-item estimates, segment/KPI consensus, Excel workflows, and data delivery, but it is not a retail all-in-one terminal, broker, or self-serve low-cost data product.

tools.name: Ideagen Audit Analytics
tools.summary: Ideagen Audit Analytics is a specialist audit, accounting, regulatory, and disclosure-risk data platform for investors, academics, and enterprise research teams. It is useful when standard fundamentals are not enough and you need structured evidence on auditor changes, audit fees, restatements, SOX control issues, going-concern opinions, SEC comment letters, PCAOB inspection signals, CAMs/KAMs, bankruptcies, IPOs, M&A, litigation, and other filing-based red flags. It is strongest as licensed diligence infrastructure, not as a retail stock screener, charting app, broker, or open public API.

tools.name: Financial Datasets
tools.summary: Financial Datasets is a developer-focused financial data API and official MCP server for teams building AI agents, stock screeners, portfolio tools, research apps, and quantitative workflows. It is strongest when you need simple programmatic access to U.S. equity fundamentals, prices, SEC filings, insider trades, institutional ownership, news, crypto prices, and screener endpoints without assembling many separate data vendors. The tradeoff is scope and licensing: coverage is centered on U.S. public companies, there is no permanent free tier, and redistribution is gated to Scale.

tools.name: Fey
tools.summary: Fey was an AI-native investing research workspace for stocks and ETFs, known for natural-language screening, AI earnings and filing summaries, personalized news, portfolio analysis, and a polished desktop-first workflow. It is no longer a current signup option: Fey joined Wealthsimple in August 2025 and its standalone service wound down on September 30, 2025. Historical context covers the former product and comparable AI investing research workflows, while current users need available alternatives.

tools.name: Snowball Analytics
tools.summary: Snowball Analytics is an EU-based portfolio and dividend tracker for retail investors who want multi-asset tracking, broker import, dividend analytics, benchmarking, fund look-through, backtesting, and mobile access. It is useful for long-term portfolio monitoring, but it is not a broker, registered investment adviser, tax filing product, or professional performance-composite system.

tools.name: Godel Terminal
tools.summary: Godel Terminal is a web-based, command-line-style financial terminal for investors and research teams that want real-time quotes, fast news, SEC filings, financial statements, options chains, institutional holders, watchlists, screeners, charts, and terminal-like workflows at a lower price than legacy terminals. It is strongest for users who want a UI-first market research workspace with published pricing and a 14-day trial. It is still not a full Bloomberg replacement for every dataset or workflow, and the public API is described as coming soon rather than generally available.

tools.name: FullRatio
tools.summary: FullRatio is a visual fundamentals and stock-ratio research site for investors who want U.S. equity screeners, TTM financials, valuation ratios, dividend metrics, fair-value charts, industry benchmarks, and simple stock comparisons. It is strongest for learning and reviewing fundamental relationships without a professional terminal: ratio pages, dashboards, price-vs-fair-value views, bubble charts, and comparisons make the data easier to scan. It is not built for intraday trading, global multi-asset coverage, public API access, or live portfolio accounting.

tools.name: AmiBroker
tools.summary: AmiBroker is a Windows desktop technical analysis and trading-system development platform for advanced traders and quants who want AFL scripting, charting, scanning, portfolio backtesting, optimization, Monte Carlo analysis, and broker/data integrations. It is strongest for serious desktop strategy research with a one-time license, but data feeds, AmiQuote, real-time quotes, and the programming learning curve are separate considerations.

tools.name: GammaWins Calculator
tools.summary: GammaWins Calculator is a free web options payoff and Greeks calculator for traders who want to model single-leg and multi-leg option strategies, visualize profit and loss, inspect Greeks, test volatility assumptions, and share strategy states. It is strongest for trade planning and education before using a broker or more advanced analytics platform. The main caveat is data latency: the calculator currently displays options and stock prices with a 15-minute delay, and planned journal, broker-sync, and paper-trading features should not be treated as broadly available.

tools.name: Uncle Stock
tools.summary: Uncle Stock is a global fundamental stock screener and screener-backtesting platform for DIY and value investors who want many financial metrics, guru-style screens, watchlists, historical backtests, CSV export, and AI/MCP stock-search access. It is strongest for long-term fundamental screening and value research, while API access, advanced backtesting, exports, crypto coverage, and unlimited MCP usage are gated to higher plans.

tools.name: BizToc
tools.summary: BizToc is a free business and finance news aggregator for investors who want a fast headline grid, real-time Wire feed, market snapshot, imagery view, search, RSS, mobile access, and a lightweight API route through RapidAPI. It is strongest for quick market-awareness and headline discovery before reading original sources, but it is an aggregator rather than original reporting, valuation research, portfolio analytics, or a full financial-data platform.

tools.name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
tools.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis is the official free source for U.S. economic accounts, including GDP, personal income, PCE inflation, industry data, international accounts, regional data, interactive tables, release calendars, downloads, and a developer API. It is strongest for macro dashboards, valuation assumptions, economic research, and data workflows that need primary-source U.S. government data, but it updates on statistical release schedules and API use requires a free UserID.

tools.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
tools.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics is the official free source for U.S. labor-market, inflation, wage, productivity, price, employment, unemployment, and occupational statistics. It is strongest for macro dashboards, CPI and jobs-report monitoring, research models, release calendars, bulk downloads, and Public Data API workflows, but BLS data updates on official statistical schedules and programmatic use requires comfort with survey structures and series IDs.

tools.name: Smartfin
tools.summary: Smartfin is a beginner-friendly U.S. stock research platform for visual financials, sector-adjusted scores, plain-English company evaluations, curated stock lists, watchlists, alerts, transcripts, filings, and research checklists. It is best for fundamental stock research without terminal complexity, not global multi-asset coverage, brokerage execution, portfolio accounting, or a public API.

tools.name: HedgeFollow
tools.summary: HedgeFollow is a web research platform for tracking hedge funds, institutional holders, insider trades, ETF activity, ownership flows, stock pages, fund pages, and portfolio-builder workflows from SEC filings. It is strongest when investors want a fast, visual way to follow 13F, 13D/13G, and Form 4 activity without paying for a larger terminal. The major caveat is timing: 13F holdings are structurally delayed by the SEC reporting process, so the data is useful for research and pattern recognition, not live portfolio mirroring.

tools.name: Tickeron
tools.summary: Tickeron is an AI-driven trading and investing platform for screeners, AI stock signals, pattern detection, paper trading, AI Robots, and short-horizon trade ideas across stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, crypto, and forex. It is useful for active idea generation and testing, but its signals and robots are not guaranteed returns, brokerage availability varies, and pricing should be checked at checkout.

tools.name: CatalystWire
tools.summary: CatalystWire is a UK-focused RNS catalyst scanner for event-driven investors who want real-time London Stock Exchange announcement monitoring, AI-powered semantic search, categorization, and instant alerts. It is strongest for finding market-moving UK announcements such as management changes, turnarounds, and other catalyst categories inside RNS flow, but public pages do not show self-serve pricing or a documented API.

tools.name: FactorsToday
tools.summary: FactorsToday is a quantitative factor-investing platform with dashboards, screeners, portfolio factor analysis, attribution, hedge construction, factor portfolio building, downloads, and an open REST API. It is useful when you need factor exposure workflows without building every model and endpoint yourself.

tools.name: Global Factor Data (JKP Factors)
tools.summary: Global Factor Data, often called JKP Factors, is a free academic research dataset and web interface for global equity factor returns, stock characteristics, and reproducible factor-construction code based on Jensen, Kelly, and Pedersen. It is best for quants, researchers, students, and factor-investing teams that need transparent evidence on global factor performance rather than marketing claims. The data is not a live trading feed, and the license is non-commercial unless separate permission is granted.

tools.name: Wall St. Rank
tools.summary: Wall St. Rank is a fund- and analyst-consensus research product for 13F manager portfolios, fund trends, analyst ratings, price targets, news sentiment, indexes, and API-accessible data. It is useful for U.S.-listed ownership and analyst research, but 13F data is delayed, API/bulk access is contact-sales, and the product is not live fund positioning or trade execution.

tools.name: CEO Watcher
tools.summary: CEO Watcher is a U.S. insider-trading discovery and alert tool for investors who want Form 4 activity ranked by insiders’ historical forward returns. It is strongest for finding high-signal insider buys and sells, unusual activity, daily pre-market briefs, real-time paid notifications, and case-study style context, but insider trades are only one input and historical insider returns do not guarantee future performance.

tools.name: Value Line
tools.summary: Value Line is a long-running investment research publisher with proprietary ranks, analyst commentary, single-page equity reports, screeners, watchlists, alerts, charting, newsletters, and separate stock, fund, ETF, option, and selection services. It is best evaluated as a subscription research service, not a modern data API, brokerage platform, or single bundled terminal.

tools.name: Value Sense
tools.summary: Value Sense is a fundamental stock research workspace for intrinsic value tools, stock ideas, screeners, backtesting, financial charts, transcripts, AI earnings summaries, smart-money tracking, dashboards, and valuation workflows. It is useful for value-oriented research, but model outputs require review, usage is plan-gated, and it is not a broker or registered investment adviser.

tools.name: Prospero.ai
tools.summary: Prospero.ai is a free mobile-first AI signal app for U.S. stocks and ETFs, with proprietary short-term and long-term signals, daily screens, stock picks, watchlists, notifications, and education. It is useful for beginner-friendly signal discovery, but it is not full fundamental research, broker sync, a web terminal, public API, or proof that a signal will work.

tools.name: Alpha Spread
tools.summary: Alpha Spread is a value-investing research platform for investors who want quick intrinsic value estimates, DCF and relative valuation, stock reports, screeners, watchlists, alerts, analyst forecasts, and AI-assisted company questions. It is strongest for first-pass fair-value research, but free usage is metered weekly and automated valuation outputs should be reviewed as assumptions, not final investment decisions.

tools.name: LuxAlgo
tools.summary: LuxAlgo is a TradingView-focused technical-analysis suite for traders who want packaged indicators, price-action overlays, screeners, alerts, oscillator tools, calculators, and AI-assisted backtesting. It is built for chart-based workflows across stocks, ETFs, futures, commodities, currencies, and crypto. It serves as a technical-analysis and strategy-exploration layer, not as a broker, fundamentals platform, portfolio accounting system, or proof that a backtest will work live.

tools.name: SpotGamma
