tools.summary: SpotGamma is an options-market microstructure platform for dealer gamma, vanna, delta, key levels, options-flow impact, volatility dashboards, heatmaps, scans, alerts, and trading-platform integrations. It is built for index, options, and intraday traders, not broad fundamental research, brokerage execution, portfolio accounting, or a public API.

tools.name: ListingTrack
tools.summary: ListingTrack is an event-driven market-intelligence platform for tracking IPOs, SPACs, de-SPACs, public M&A, pre-IPO pipelines, listing events, and related themes. It is useful for investors who want structured listing-event data and watchlist workflows that generic news feeds can miss. It is not a full fundamentals terminal, valuation modeler, broker, portfolio accounting system, or unrestricted data API.

tools.name: StockAlert Pro
tools.summary: StockAlert Pro is an alert-first stock and ETF monitoring platform with configurable alerts, watchlists, AI equity reports, API keys, webhooks, SDKs, and integrations. It is useful when investors or builders need notifications and automation around price, technical, volume, fundamental, dividend, and time conditions, but it is not a broker, full research terminal, or portfolio accounting system.

tools.name: FinancialJuice
tools.summary: FinancialJuice is a live market news and squawk service for traders who need fast audio headlines, real-time text updates, macro calendar context, and market-moving event alerts across equities, rates, FX, commodities, crypto, and futures. Developers can also consume news headlines and economic-calendar events as JSON through the documented WebSocket Stream API. It is strongest for time-to-awareness around economic releases, central-bank news, geopolitical headlines, and session prep rather than deep valuation work. Free access exists, but real-time web, mobile, and API workflows depend on the relevant paid plan.

tools.name: BuySide Digest - Hedge Fund Letter Database
tools.summary: BuySide Digest - Hedge Fund Letter Database is a free research database for investors who want to search hedge-fund letters, manager commentary, tickers, themes, quarters, 13F context, and curated investment pitches. It is strongest for qualitative idea discovery from public manager letters and follow-up alerts, but coverage depends on available public documents and letters are delayed, opinionated commentary rather than live recommendations.

tools.name: Multpl
tools.summary: Multpl is a free reference site for long-run S&P 500 valuation, earnings, dividends, Treasury rates, real yields, CPI, inflation, GDP, population, and income charts. It is useful for quick macro and index-valuation context, but it is not a company screener, portfolio tracker, real-time trading feed, or first-party developer API.

tools.name: CEO.CA
tools.summary: CEO.CA is a Canadian small-cap investor community and market-data platform for traders and investors following TSX, TSXV, and CSE issuers. It is strongest for ticker chat rooms, watchlists, real-time news, SEDI insider filings, private placements, audience analytics, mobile access, and paid Level II market depth, but community posts are not research and Pro pricing depends on which Canadian exchanges you need.

tools.name: Valuesider
tools.summary: Valuesider is a free web tool for tracking superinvestor portfolios, aggregated guru holdings, recent buys and sells, and security ownership based on SEC 13F filings. It is useful for value-investor idea generation, but 13F data is delayed and incomplete, history starts at 2013 Q2, and the site does not grant automated scraping or bulk-data rights.

tools.name: Journalytic
tools.summary: Journalytic is an investment journal and decision-process analytics workspace for investors who want to record ideas, thesis changes, checklists, predictions, moods, self-contracts, and postmortems in one place. It is useful for improving investment process quality over time, especially when users want more structure than a notes app but do not need a trading journal built around execution logs. Open beta access is currently free, but it is not a market-data terminal, screener, broker, or research database.

tools.name: This Is Not SEDAR
tools.summary: This Is Not SEDAR is an independent research interface for Canadian filings, financial results, company news, prospectuses, and SEDI insider activity. It can speed up discovery and company research, but official SEDAR+ remains the source of record; full search requires sign-in, and no public API or uptime SLA is published.

tools.name: Capitol Trades
tools.summary: Capitol Trades is a free public web app from 2iQ Research for tracking U.S. politician trading disclosures under the STOCK Act. It is strongest for investors, journalists, and researchers who want to filter congressional trades by politician, issuer, chamber, party, committee, state, asset type, transaction type, sector, size range, and filing details, but disclosure timing can lag trades and reported amounts are ranges rather than exact fills.

tools.name: Insider Monitor
tools.summary: Insider Monitor is a free U.S. insider-trading reference site for tracking SEC Forms 3, 4, and 5 across insider purchases, sales, officer cluster buys, and top insider-buying lists. It is useful as a quick, no-login way to spot recent Form 4 activity and then jump back to the original SEC filing. Because insiders can report trades after the transaction date and the site does not advertise alerts, exports, or an API, it should be treated as a lightweight research prompt rather than a complete monitoring system.

tools.name: Dilution Tracker
tools.summary: Dilution Tracker is a small-cap research tool for monitoring share-supply risk from shelves, ATMs, warrants, convertibles, S-1 offerings, reverse splits, and related filings. It is useful when dilution risk can make or break a trade, especially in volatile U.S. small-cap names.

tools.name: RetailRoadshow
tools.summary: RetailRoadshow is a NetRoadshow-operated portal for viewing SEC-compliant electronic roadshow videos and prospectus materials for registered public offerings, primarily IPOs. It is useful for hearing issuer management presentations during active offerings, but access depends on availability, registration, and sometimes deal-specific entry codes.

tools.name: InsideArbitrage
tools.summary: InsideArbitrage is a paid event-driven investing research platform for merger arbitrage, insider transactions, spinoffs, buybacks, CVRs, tender offers, activist campaigns, and other special situations. It combines screens, trackers, calendars, deal updates, newsletters, and portfolio/watchlist workflows for investors who actively follow corporate events. It is not a broad fundamentals terminal, broker, portfolio accounting system, or public market-data API.

tools.name: FinancialReports.eu
tools.summary: Financial Filings is a public-company filings database, filings API, and hosted MCP server for analysts, AI-agent builders, and data teams that need fast document ingestion, Markdown extraction, watchlist alerts, webhooks, and filing Q&A across global markets. It is strongest when the workflow starts with filings rather than price charts: company documents, insider trades, IPO references, filing feeds, and programmatic document access are the center of the product. The web index is free to browse, while serious API, MCP, webhook, redistribution, and production workflows are contact-sales.

tools.name: FOIAsearch
tools.summary: FOIAsearch is a free SEC FOIA log search and alert product for investors, journalists, short sellers, and investor-relations teams watching for regulatory or reporter attention around public companies. It is strongest as an early-warning research signal: SEC FOIA requests, B7A exemption denials, portfolio alerts, IR Watch, and prominent-reporter alerts can prompt deeper due diligence before a story or enforcement signal becomes widely visible. The output is indirect evidence, not proof of wrongdoing, and paid alert pricing is not publicly listed.

tools.name: r/SecurityAnalysis - Letters Wiki
tools.summary: The r/SecurityAnalysis Letters Wiki is a free, community-maintained reading list of investor letters, hedge fund letters, fund reports, and related quarterly threads. It is useful for idea generation and learning from manager commentary, but it is not a structured data product, archive guarantee, alerting system, or extracted fundamentals database.

tools.name: EPSMomentum
tools.summary: EPSMomentum is a U.S. stock and ETF analytics platform for earnings momentum, estimate revisions, PEAD drift, timing signals, scanners, AI analysis, and market dashboards. It is useful when earnings acceleration and entry-timing discipline are central to your research process.

tools.name: TickerTrends
tools.summary: TickerTrends is an alternative-data and KPI-forecasting platform for public-company investors, analysts, quant teams, hedge funds, and institutions. It combines search, web traffic, app usage, social, reviews, news, transcripts, financial data, consensus, and proprietary trend signals, but those signals are noisy proxies that require validation before investment use.

tools.name: Databento
tools.summary: Databento supplies normalized live and historical exchange data through APIs, files, and client libraries. It is built for developers, quants, and trading firms that need tick data, full order books, bars, instrument definitions, corporate actions, or raw packet captures across supported equity, options, and futures venues.

tools.name: FINRA Fixed Income Data
tools.summary: FINRA Fixed Income Data is an official source for U.S. bond security details, disseminated TRACE transactions, trade-activity history, and aggregate market reports. It is useful for researching executed prices and volumes, but TRACE is not a quote system, exchange, or execution venue.

tools.name: Cbonds
tools.summary: Cbonds is a global bond-data and research platform for professional and private investors. Its core workflow combines bond search, quotes, yields, ratings, new-issue and event calendars, watchlists, and portfolio tools; company clients can also license APIs, files, and an Excel add-in.

tools.name: EIA Open Data
tools.summary: EIA Open Data is the U.S. government source for statistical and operational energy data. Analysts and developers can browse energy series or retrieve them through a free API, bulk files, and spreadsheet tools for macro, commodity, utility, and energy-market research.

tools.name: Option Alpha
tools.summary: Option Alpha helps retail options traders find ideas, backtest rule-based strategies, paper trade, and automate supported stock and risk-defined options workflows through connected brokers. It is software rather than a broker, and live trading depends on broker, account, symbol, strategy, and jurisdiction support.

tools.name: EMMA
tools.summary: EMMA is the official public transparency platform for the U.S. municipal-securities market. It brings together disseminated trade prices, offering documents, continuing disclosures, credit ratings, issuer information, new-issue calendars, alerts, and market statistics for municipal-bond research.

tools.name: Barchart cmdtyView
tools.summary: Barchart cmdtyView combines exchange-traded futures data, physical commodity pricing, charting, news, analytics, economic data, and connected commodity workflows. It is designed for commercial, agricultural, energy, metals, trading, procurement, and risk teams rather than general stock research.

tools.name: EDINET
tools.summary: EDINET is Japan's official electronic corporate-disclosure system. It supports issuer, security, fund, stock-code, document-type, keyword, and date searches, with source filings, XBRL resources, taxonomy files, and an API for programmatic filing retrieval.

tools.name: ShareScope
tools.summary: ShareScope combines stock and fund research, screening, charting, news, alerts, and portfolio management for private investors, with an emphasis on UK markets and additional U.S., Canadian, and European coverage. ShareScope Pro adds real-time LSE Level 2 features.

tools.name: rotki
tools.summary: rotki is a privacy-focused portfolio tracker and accounting tool that runs on the user's own machine. It combines exchange and blockchain activity, decodes on-chain events, tracks balances and history, and produces configurable profit-and-loss and tax reports without requiring transaction history to live in a hosted tax service.

tools.name: ProjectionLab
tools.summary: ProjectionLab is a web-based financial and retirement planning simulator for mapping income, spending, investments, major life events, financial independence, and estate outcomes over time. Users can compare what-if plans, run Monte Carlo simulations and historical backtests, and inspect annual cash-flow and estimated-tax results. The free Basic plan covers forecasting and core simulations; Premium adds deeper cash-flow, tax, withdrawal, reporting, and multi-plan tools, while Pro adds client management for advisors and coaches. It is a manual planning model, not a live account aggregator, brokerage, or substitute for professional advice.

tools.name: Wealthfolio
tools.summary: Wealthfolio is a free, open-source, local-first portfolio and personal-finance app for investors who want holdings, performance, allocation, income, net worth, spending, goals, rebalancing, and retirement planning in a SQLite database they control. It runs on macOS, Windows, Linux, and iOS or as a self-hosted web app. Optional Wealthfolio Connect plans add encrypted device sync and read-only brokerage imports, while manual tracking and CSV import remain free without an account.

tools.name: TradeLog
tools.summary: TradeLog is Windows desktop trade-accounting software for U.S. active traders who need to consolidate complete trade history, identify taxpayer-level wash sales across accounts and IRAs, reconcile proceeds, and prepare reports for a tax return or tax professional. Its differentiated workflow covers Form 8949, supported Sections 1256 and 475 reporting, tax-lot adjustments, and year-round wash-sale monitoring. It does not import Form 1099-B, file a return, provide tax advice, execute trades, or offer complete current digital-asset reporting.

tools.name: StreamXLS
tools.summary: StreamXLS is a Windows-only Excel RTD bridge for investors and trading desks that want their own Interactive Brokers quotes, account values, positions, live P&L, and open-order state inside spreadsheet formulas. It runs locally through TWS or IB Gateway and can stage an order ticket for manual review in TWS, but it does not transmit trades, include market-data entitlements, support Mac or browser Excel, or replace IBKR. The product is closed source and its public release history began only recently.
